<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A tin of paint can cover $45 \ \text{m}^2$ of wall. The school hall has $652 \ \text{m}^2$ of wall to paint.

How many tins of paint are needed?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A tin of paint can cover $45 \ \text{m}^2$ of wall. The school hall has $652 \ \text{m}^2$ of wall to paint.
<emptyline>
How many tins of paint are needed?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of tins needed}  &= \dfrac {\text{Total area of the hall}} {\text{Area covered by a tin}} \\\\
                               &= \dfrac {652} {45} \\\\
                               &= 14.48 \\\\
                               &= 15
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$15$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A triangle has a base of $6 \ \text{cm}$ and a height 
of $4 \ \text{cm}$. It has the same area as another
triangle of base length $8 \ \text{cm}$. How tall is the triangle?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A triangle has a base of $6 \ \text{cm}$ and a height 
of $4 \ \text{cm}$. It has the same area as another
triangle of base length $8 \ \text{cm}$. How tall is the triangle?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the height of the second triangle $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {1} {2} \times 8 \ \times a        &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 6 \ \times 4 \\\\
\dfrac {8} {2} \times a                   &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 24 \\\\
a                                         &= \dfrac {24} {2} \times \dfrac {2} {8} \\\\
a                                         &= \dfrac {24 \times 2} {2 \times 8} \\\\
a                                         &= \dfrac {3 \times 8 \times 2} {2 \times 8} \\\\
a                                         &= \dfrac {3 \times \cancel {8} \times \cancel {2}} {\cancel {2} \times \cancel {8}} \\\\
a                                         &= 3 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Triangle is $3 \ \text{cm}$ tall.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$3 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

I have a square piece of paper.

![papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s02-q11-s01-i00.png](/assets/papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s02-q11-s01-i00.png "papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s02-q11-s01-i00.png")

I fold square $A$ in half to make rectangle $B$.

![papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s02-q11-s01-i01.png](/assets/papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s02-q11-s01-i01.png "papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s02-q11-s01-i01.png")

Then I fold rectangle $B$ in half to make square $C$.

![papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s02-q11-s01-i02.png](/assets/papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s02-q11-s01-i02.png "papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s02-q11-s01-i02.png")

Complete the table below to show the area and perimeter of each shape.

|               |         Area         |      Perimenter    |
|:-------------:|:--------------------:|:------------------:|
| Square $A$    | $\ldots \ \text{cm}^2$ | $\ldots \ \text{cm}$ |
| Rectangle $B$ | $\ldots \ \text{cm}^2$ | $\ldots \ \text{cm}$ |
| Square $C$    | $\ldots \ \text{cm}^2$ | $\ldots \ \text{cm}$ |

</div>

\end{aligned}

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The diagram shows a square with a perimeter of $12 \ \text{cm}$.

![papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s03-q01-i00.png](/assets/papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s03-q01-i00.png "papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s03-q01-i00.png")

Six of these squares fit together to make a rectangle.

![papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s03-q01-i01.png](/assets/papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s03-q01-i01.png "papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s03-q01-i01.png")

What is the area of the rectangle?

You must give the correct unit with your answer. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The diagram shows a square with a perimeter of $12 \ \text{cm}$.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
Six of these squares fit together to make a rectangle.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
What is the area of the rectangle?
<emptyline>
You must give the correct unit with your answer. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of the square}      &= 12 \times 12 \\\\
                                &= 144 \ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
\text {Area of the rectangle}   &= 6 \times \text {Area of a sqaure} \\\\
                                &= 6 \times 144 \\\\
                                &= 864 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$864 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>

**Question**

The perimeter of a regular hexagon is $42a + 18$.

Write an expression for the length of one of its sides.

![papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s03-q06-s01-i00.png](/assets/papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s03-q06-s01-i00.png "papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-2/s03-q06-s01-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The perimeter of a regular hexagon is $42a + 18$.
<emptyline>
Write an expression for the length of one of its sides.
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of the hexagon $= s$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
6 \times s  &= 42a + 18 \\\\
6s          &= 42a + 18 \\\\
s           &= \dfrac {42a + 18} {6} \\\\
s           &= \dfrac {6 \times 7a + 6 \times 3} {6} \\\\
s           &= \dfrac {6 \times (7a + 3)} {6} \\\\
s           &= \dfrac {\cancel {6} \times (7a + 3)} {\cancel {6}} \\\\
s           &= 7a + 3
\end{aligned}
$

Length of the one side of hexagon $= 7a + 3$.
</div>

**Question**

The perimeter of a different regular polygon is $75b - 20$.

The length of one of its sides is $15b - 4$.

How many sides does this regular polygon have?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The perimeter of a different regular polygon is $75b - 20$.
<emptyline>
The length of one of its sides is $15b - 4$.
<emptyline>
How many sides does this regular polygon have?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of regular polygon} = \text{n} \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of sides in polygon $= n$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
n \times (15b - 4)  &= 75b - 20 \\\\
n                   &= \dfrac {75b - 20} {15b - 4} \\\\
n                   &= \dfrac {5 \times 15b - 5 \times 4} {15b - 4} \\\\
n                   &= \dfrac {5 \times (15b - 4)} {15b - 4} \\\\
n                   &= \dfrac {5 \times (\cancel {15b - 4})} {\cancel {15b - 4}} \\\\
n                   &= 5
\end{aligned}
$

The regular polygon has 5 sides.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

5

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The perimeter of a square is $4(c - 9)$.

Find the area of the square when $c = 15$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The perimeter of a square is $4(c - 9)$.
<emptyline>
Find the area of the square when $c = 15$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of the sqaure $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
4 \times a         &= 4(c - 9) \\\\
4a                 &= 4 \times (c - 9) \\\\
a                  &= \dfrac {4 \times (c - 9)} {4} \\\\
a                  &= \dfrac {\cancel {4} \times (c - 9)} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
a                  &= c - 9 \\\\
a                  &= 15 - 9 \\\\
a                  &= 6 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the area of the square.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area}            &= a \times a \\\\
                        &= 6 \times 6 \\\\
                        &= 36 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$36 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

My other friend Minka was doing some gardening when she snapped a bamboo cane. The cane was $2.05 \ \text{m}$ long and is now 
$156 \ \text{cm}$ long. What length of cane snapped off?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">My other friend Minka was doing some gardening when she snapped a bamboo cane. The cane was $2.05 \ \text{m}$ long and is now 
$156 \ \text{cm}$ long. What length of cane snapped off?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
_no_dot
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The original length is given in $\text{meters}$ while the new length measurement is given in $\text{cm}$.

Let's convert the original measurements into $\text{cm}$.

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Original length of cane}         &= 2.05 \ \text{m} \\\\
                                        &= 2.05 \times 100 \ \text{cm} \\\\
                                        &= 2.05 \times 100 \\\\
                                        &= 205 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Legth of the cane snapped off}   &= \text {Original Length} - \text {New Length} \\\\
                                        &= 205 - 156 \\\\
                                        &= 49 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$49 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

In her garden, Ying-Ge is sowing some grass seed. The garden has an area of $158 \ \text{m}^2$ and each packet has enough seed for 
$12 \ \text{m}^2$. How many packets does Ying-Ge need to buy?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In her garden, Ying-Ge is sowing some grass seed. The garden has an area of $158 \ \text{m}^2$ and each packet has enough seed for 
$12 \ \text{m}^2$. How many packets does Ying-Ge need to buy?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of packets}   &= \dfrac {\text {Area of the garden}} {\text {Area per packet of seeds}} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {158} {12} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {12 \times 14} {12} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {\cancel {12} \times 14} {\cancel {12}} \\\\
                            &= 14
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

14

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

On my wall I want to put some stickers of David Cameron. The space I have available is $80 \ \text{cm}$ by $45 \ \text{cm}$ 
and the stickers are each $5 \ \text{cm}$ by $10 \ \text{cm}$. What is the maximum number of stickers I can fit on the wall?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">On my wall I want to put some stickers of David Cameron. The space I have available is $80 \ \text{cm}$ by $45 \ \text{cm}$ 
and the stickers are each $5 \ \text{cm}$ by $10 \ \text{cm}$. What is the maximum number of stickers I can fit on the wall?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of stickers}  &= \dfrac {\text{Area of the wall}} {\text{Area of a sticker}} \\\\
                           &= \dfrac {80 \times 45} {10 \times 5} \\\\
                           &= \dfrac {8 \times 10 \times 5 \times 9} {10 \times 5} \\\\
                           &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel {10} \times \cancel {5} \times 9} {\cancel {10} \times \cancel {5}} \\\\
                           &= 8 \times 9 \\\\
                           &= 72
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

72

</div>
</div>

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">As per the question,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of stickers}  &= \dfrac {\text{Area of the wall}} {\text{Area of a sticker}} \\\\
                           &= \dfrac {80 \times 45} {10 \times 5} \\\\
                           &= \dfrac {8 \times 10 \times 5 \times 9} {10 \times 5} \\\\
                           &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel {10} \times \cancel {5} \times 9} {\cancel {10} \times \cancel {5}} \\\\
                           &= 8 \times 9 \\\\
                           &= 72
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>

**Question**

The total length of the edges of a cube is $240 \ \text{cm}$. What is the length of one edge?

![papers/bancrofts-school/2013/sample-paper-1/s01-q16-i00.png](/assets/papers/bancrofts-school/2013/sample-paper-1/s01-q16-i00.png "papers/bancrofts-school/2013/sample-paper-1/s01-q16-i00.png")

<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The total length of the edges of a cube is $240 \ \text{cm}$. What is the length of one edge?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Total number of edges in a cube $= 12$

Let the edge of the cube $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
12 \times a &= 240 \\\\
a           &= \dfrac {240} {12} \\\\
a           &= \dfrac {12 \times 20} {12} \\\\
a           &= \dfrac { \cancel {12} \times 20} {\cancel {12}} \\\\
a           &= 20 \ \text{cm} 
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$20 \ \text{cm} $

</div>

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Who has the largest square?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Who has the largest square?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of Vikram's square}             &= 64 \ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
\text {Area of Kim's square}                &= 64 \times 64 \\\\
                                            &= 4096 \ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
\text {Let the side of the Ali's square}    &= a \\\\
4 \times a                                  &= 64 \\\\
a                                           &= \dfrac {64} {4} \\\\
a                                           &= \dfrac {4 \times 16} {4} \\\\
a                                           &= \dfrac {\cancel {4} \times 16} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
a                                           &= 16 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Area of Ali's square}                &= a \times a \\\\
                                            &= 16 \times 16 \\\\
                                            &= 256 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$

Ali has the largest square.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Ali

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The area of a right angled triangle is $32 \ \text{cm}^{2}$.

The lengths, in $\text{cm}$, of the two shorter sides are both different square numbers bigger than $1$.

What are the lengths of the two shorter sides?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The area of a right angled triangle is $32 \ \text{cm}^{2}$.
<emptyline>
The lengths, in $\text{cm}$, of the two shorter sides are both different square numbers bigger than $1$.
<emptyline>
What are the lengths of the two shorter sides?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the height of the triangle $= h$

Let the base of the triangle $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {1} {2} \times b \times h    &= 32 \\\\
\dfrac {b \times h} {2}             &= 32 \\\\
b \times h                          &= 32 \times 2 \\\\
b \times h                          &= 64
\end{aligned}
$

Factors of $64 = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64$

Factor pairs of $64$ that are both different square numbers $ = 4, 16$

Length of the two shorter sides are $4 \ \text{cm}$ and $16 \ \text{cm}$.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4 \ \text{cm} \ , 16 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

What is the area of one face of the cube?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the area of one face of the cube?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Surface area of cube} = 6 \times \text{edge} \times \text{edge}$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of one face of cube} = \text{edge} \times \text{edge}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the edge of the cube $= a$ 

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
6 \times a \times a                       &= 96 \\\\
6 \times a^2                              &= 96 \\\\
a^2                                       &= \dfrac {96} {6} \\\\
a^2                                       &= \dfrac {6 \times 16} {6} \\\\
a^2                                       &= \dfrac {\cancel {6} \times 16} {\cancel {6}} \\\\
a^2                                       &= 16 \\\\
a                                         &= \sqrt {16} \\\\
a                                         &= 4 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the area of one face of the cube.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of once face}       &= a \times a \\\\
                                &= 4 \times 4 \\\\
                                &= 16 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Yusuf has $6$ equilateral triangles, each with a perimeter of $12 \ \text{cm}$.

He fits them together to make a regular hexagon.

What is the hexagon's perimeter?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Yusuf has $6$ equilateral triangles, each with a perimeter of $12 \ \text{cm}$.
<emptyline>
He fits them together to make a regular hexagon.
<emptyline>
What is the hexagon's perimeter?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of triangle} = 3 \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of polygon} = \text{Sum of all sides}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

*ABBR: TODO:: Add drawing starts.*

{/* ![missing image](/papers/missing_image.svg) */}
TODOIMAGE


*TODO:: Add two diagram a small equilateral triangle and a hexagon which is made by adding 6 small ones.
Show each side of hexagon is equal to triangle.*

*ABBR: TODO:: Add drawing ends.*


Let the side of equilateral triangle $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
3 \times a          &= 12 \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {12} {3} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {3 \times 4} {3} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {3} \times 4} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                   &= 4 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Side of hexagon}                 &= a \\\\
                                        &= 4 \ \text{cm}\\\\
\text {Perimeter of hexagon}            &= 6 \times a \\\\
                                        &= 24 \ \text{cm}                                        
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$24 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

\end{aligned}

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A rectangle measuring $7 \ \text{cm}$ by $6 \ \text{cm}$ overlaps 
a rectangle measuring $9 \ \text{cm}$ by $8 \ \text{cm}$ as shown in the diagram.

The region shaded grey has an area of $32 \ \text{cm}^2$.

What is the area of the black region?

![papers/bancrofts-school/2016/sample-paper-2/s01-q29-i00.png](/assets/papers/bancrofts-school/2016/sample-paper-2/s01-q29-i00.png "papers/bancrofts-school/2016/sample-paper-2/s01-q29-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A rectangle measuring $7 \ \text{cm}$ by $6 \ \text{cm}$ overlaps 
a rectangle measuring $9 \ \text{cm}$ by $8 \ \text{cm}$ as shown in the diagram.
<emptyline>
The region shaded grey has an area of $32 \ \text{cm}^2$.
<emptyline>
What is the area of the black region?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Overlapped Area}         &= \text {Area of smaller rectangle} - \text {Area of grey region} \\\\
                                &= 7 \times 6 - 32 \\\\
                                &= 42 - 32 \\\\
                                &= 8 \ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
\text {Area of black region}    &= \text {Area of larger rectangle} - \text {Overlapped Area} \\\\
                                &= 9 \times 8 - 8 \\\\
                                &= 72 - 8 \\\\
                                &= 64 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$64 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of one tile}            &= \dfrac {\text {Area of the cross}} {\text {Number of tiles}} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {245} {5} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {49 \times 5} {5} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {49 \times \cancel {5}} {\cancel {5}} \\\\
                                    &= 49 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

It takes $9 \ \text{litres}$ of paint to cover the surface of the cube on the left.

![papers/bancrofts-school/2017/sample-paper-3/s01-q21-i00.png](/assets/papers/bancrofts-school/2017/sample-paper-3/s01-q21-i00.png "papers/bancrofts-school/2017/sample-paper-3/s01-q21-i00.png")

How many litres of paint would it take to cover the surface of the shape on the right?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">It takes $9 \ \text{litres}$ of paint to cover the surface of the cube on the left.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
How many litres of paint would it take to cover the surface of the shape on the right?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of faces painted}           &= 9 \times 6  \\\\
                                          &= 54 \\\\
\text {Litres required to paint one face} &= \dfrac {9} {54} \\\\ 
                                          &= \dfrac {9} {9 \times 6} \\\\
                                          &= \dfrac {\cancel 9} {\cancel 9 \times 6} \\\\ 
                                          &= \dfrac {1} {6} \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of faces to be painted}     &= 9 \times 3 + 5 \times 3 + 4 \times 3  \\\\
                                          &= 54 \\\\
\text {Litres required to paint 54 face}  &= \dfrac {1} {6} \times 54 \\\\ 
                                          &= \dfrac {1} {6} \times 9 \times 6\\\\
                                          &= \dfrac {1} {\cancel 6} \times 9 \times \cancel 6\\\\ 
                                          &= 9 \ \text{litres} \\\\
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$9 \ \text{litres}$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

Buildings take up $\dfrac{3}{5}$ of the area. How much area is this?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Buildings take up $\dfrac{3}{5}$ of the area. How much area is this?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of Building}            &= \dfrac {3} {5} \times \text {Area of site} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {3} {5} \times 8000 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {3 \times 8000} {5} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {3 \times 5 \times 1600} {5} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {3 \times \cancel {5} \times 1600} {\cancel {5}} \\\\
                                    &= 3 \times 1600 \\\\
                                    &= 4800 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

**Working**

As per the question,

$

a                                                   &= 150 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the area of the grass.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of the grass}   &= 7 \times a \\\\
                            &= 7 \times 150 \\\\
                            &= 1050 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$

edges $1 \ \text{cm}$ long, how many smaller cubes can be made?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Volume of a cube} = (\text{Side}) ^ { 3 }$
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Volume of 2 cm cube}      &= 2 \times 2 \times 2 \\\\
                                &= 8 \ \text{cm}^3 \\\\
\text{Volume of 1 cm cube}      &= 1 \times 1 \times 1 \\\\
                                &= 1 \ \text{cm}^3 \\\\
\text{Number of smaller cubes}  &= \dfrac {8} {1} \\\\
                                &= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                                &= 8 \ \text{cm}^3 \\\\
\text{Volume of 1 cm cube}      &= 1 \times 1 \times 1 \\\\
                                &= 1 \ \text{cm}^3 \\\\
\text{Number of smaller cubes}  &= \dfrac {8} {1} \\\\
                                &= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A rectangular garden is surrounded by a path of a fixed width.

The perimeter of the garden is $24 \ \text{metres}$ **less** than the 
distance along the outside edge of the path.

What is the width of the path?

![papers/bancrofts-school/2017/sample-paper-3/s01-q29-i00.png](/assets/papers/bancrofts-school/2017/sample-paper-3/s01-q29-i00.png "papers/bancrofts-school/2017/sample-paper-3/s01-q29-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A rectangular garden is surrounded by a path of a fixed width.
<emptyline>
The perimeter of the garden is $24 \ \text{metres}$ **less** than the 
distance along the outside edge of the path.
<emptyline>
What is the width of the path?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the width of the path $= a$

Let the length of the garden $= l$

Let the width of the garden $= w$

Length of outside edge of the path $= l + a$

Width of outside edge of the path $= w + a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times ((l + a) + (w + a)) - 24   &= 2 \times (l + w) \\\\
2 \times (l + w + 2a) - 24          &= 2 \times (l + w) \\\\
2l + 2w + 4a - 24                   &= 2l + 2w \\\\
4a                                  &= 2l + 2w - 2l -  2w + 24 \\\\
4a                                  &= 24 \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {24} {4} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {4 \times 6} {4} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {4} \times 6} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
a                                   &= 6 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Width of the path $= 6 \ \text{cm}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$6 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

A square has a perimeter of $20 \ \text{cm}$. 

What is the square's area?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A square has a perimeter of $20 \ \text{cm}$. 
<emptyline>
What is the square's area?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of the square $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
4 \times a          &= 20 \\\\
4a                  &= 20 \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {20} {4} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {4 \times 5} {4} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {4} \times 5} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
a                   &= 5 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the area of the square.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area}            &= a \times a \\\\
                        &= 5 \times 5 \\\\
                        &= 25 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$25 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

A rectangle has a perimeter of $20 \ \text{cm}$. 

Its length is $2 \ \text{cm}$ longer than its width. 

What is the rectangle's area?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A rectangle has a perimeter of $20 \ \text{cm}$. 
<emptyline>
Its length is $2 \ \text{cm}$ longer than its width. 
<emptyline>
What is the rectangle's area?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the width of the rectangle $= w$

Length of the rectangle $= w + 2$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times (w + (w + 2))          &= 20 \\\\
2 \times (2w + 2)               &= 20 \\\\
4w + 4                          &= 20 \\\\
4w                              &= 20 - 4 \\\\
4w                              &= 16 \\\\
w                               &= \dfrac {16} {4} \\\\
w                               &= \dfrac {4 \times 4} {4} \\\\
w                               &= \dfrac {\cancel {4} \times 4} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
w                               &= 4 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Length}                  &= 4 + 2 \\\\
                                &= 6 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Area}                    &= 4 \times 6 \\\\
                                &= 24 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$24 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the width of the rectangle $= w$

<emptyline>

2 \times (w + 4w)               &= 20 \\\\

w                               &= \dfrac {20} {10} \\\\
w                               &= \dfrac {10 \times 2} {10} \\\\
w                               &= \dfrac {\cancel {10} \times 2} {\cancel {10}} \\\\
w                               &= 2 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Length}                  &= 4 \times 2 \\\\
                                &= 8 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Area}                    &= 2 \times 8 \\\\
                                &= 16 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}

What is the square's perimeter?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Another square has an area of $81 \ \text{cm}^2$.

<div class="workings">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of the square $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times a          &= 81 \\\\
a^2                 &= 81 \\\\
a                   &= \sqrt {81} \\\\
a                   &= 9 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the perimeter of the square.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Perimeter}       &= 4 \times a \\\\
                        &= 4 \times 9 \\\\
                        &= 36 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Question**

If the figure shown is folded to form a cube, then three faces meet at every vertex (corner).

![papers/bancrofts-school/2021/sample-paper-7/s01-q38-s01-i00.png](/assets/papers/bancrofts-school/2021/sample-paper-7/s01-q38-s01-i00.png "papers/bancrofts-school/2021/sample-paper-7/s01-q38-s01-i00.png")

The numbers on the three faces meeting at any vertex can be multiplied together.

What is the largest such product for the vertices of this cube?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A square floor is tiled with square tiles and there are $77$ tiles on the diagonals.

![papers/bancrofts-school/2021/sample-paper-7/s01-q38-s02-i00.png](/assets/papers/bancrofts-school/2021/sample-paper-7/s01-q38-s02-i00.png "papers/bancrofts-school/2021/sample-paper-7/s01-q38-s02-i00.png") 

The diagram shows part of the floor. 

How many tiles are in the room?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A square floor is tiled with square tiles and there are $77$ tiles on the diagonals.
<emptyline>
%image% 
<emptyline>
The diagram shows part of the floor. 
<emptyline>
How many tiles are in the room?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the diagram

Let the number of tiles till the middle of diagonal $=a$ 

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of tiles in the diagonal} &= 4 \times a + 1 \\\\
4 \times a + 1                         &= 77 \\\\
4 \times a                             &= 77 - 1 \\\\
4 \times a                             &= 76 \\\\
a                                      &= \dfrac {76} {4} \\\\
a                                      &= \dfrac {19 \times 4} {4} \\\\
a                                      &= \dfrac {19 \times \cancel 4} {\cancel 4} \\\\
a                                      &= 19
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Total tiles on the edges} &= 2 \times a + 1 \\\\
                                &= 2 \times 19 + 1 \\\\
                                &= 39
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Total number of tiles}    &= 39 \times 39 \\\\
                                &= 1521 
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$1521$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

If the area of each square is $9 \ \text{cm}^2$, what is the outer perimeter of the whole shape? The diagram is not drawn to scale.

![papers/chigwell-school/2020/sample-paper-1/s01-q12-i00.png](/assets/papers/chigwell-school/2020/sample-paper-1/s01-q12-i00.png "papers/chigwell-school/2020/sample-paper-1/s01-q12-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If the area of each square is $9 \ \text{cm}^2$, what is the outer perimeter of the whole shape? The diagram is not drawn to scale.
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the length of a side of the square (in $\text{cm}$) $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times a          &= 9 \\\\
a^2                 &= 9 \\\\
a                   &= \sqrt {9} \\\\
a                   &= 3 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Length of the rectangle (in cm)}  &= 3 \times a \\\\
                                         &= 3 \times 3 \\\\
                                         &= 9 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Width of the rectangle (in cm)}   &= a \\\\
                                         &= 3 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Total Perimeter}                   &= 2 \times (9 + 3) \\\\
                                         &= 2 \times 12 \\\\
                                         &= 24 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$24 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

- rtq_abbr_formula_katex_expanded_perimeter_rectangle
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<emptyline>
As per the question,

$

                                         &= 3 \ \text{cm} \\\\

                                         &= 2 \times 12 \\\\
                                         &= 24 \ \text{cm}

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is the area of the shaded part of the rectangle below?

![papers/chigwell-school/2020/sample-paper-1/s01-q18-i00.png](/assets/papers/chigwell-school/2020/sample-paper-1/s01-q18-i00.png "papers/chigwell-school/2020/sample-paper-1/s01-q18-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the area of the shaded part of the rectangle below?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

*ABBR: TODO:: Add drawing ends.*


Let the base of the first triangle $= a$

Let the base of the first triangle $= b$

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of the shaded part}         &= \text {Rectangle} - (\text {Triangle 1} + \text {Triangle 2}) \\\\
                                        &= 6 \times 16 - (\dfrac {1} {2} \times a \times 6 + \dfrac {1} {2} \times b \times 6) \\\\ 
                                        &= 6 \times 16 - \dfrac {1} {2} \times 6 \times (a + b) \\\\ 
                                        &= 6 \times 16 - \dfrac {1} {2} \times 6 \times 16 \\\\ 
                                        &= 6 \times 16 - \dfrac {6 \times 16} {2} \\\\ 
                                        &= 6 \times 16 - \dfrac {2 \times 3 \times 16} {2} \\\\ 
                                        &= 6 \times 16 - \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 3 \times 16} {\cancel {2}} \\\\ 
                                        &= 6 \times 16 - 3 \times 16 \\\\ 
                                        &= 96 - 48 \\\\ 
                                        &= 48 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$48 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>

![papers/city-of-london-school/2008/sample-paper-group-2/s01-q11-s01-i00.png](/assets/papers/city-of-london-school/2008/sample-paper-group-2/s01-q11-s01-i00.png "papers/city-of-london-school/2008/sample-paper-group-2/s01-q11-s01-i00.png")

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The diagram below shows a rectangle and a square. The diagrams are not drawn to scale.

![papers/city-of-london-school/2020/sample-paper-1/s01-q12-i00.png](/assets/papers/city-of-london-school/2020/sample-paper-1/s01-q12-i00.png "papers/city-of-london-school/2020/sample-paper-1/s01-q12-i00.png")

If they have equal perimeters, what is the difference in their area? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The diagram below shows a rectangle and a square. The diagrams are not drawn to scale.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
If they have equal perimeters, what is the difference in their area? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of square $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
4a   &= 70 + 30 + 70 + 30 \\\\
4a   &= 200 \\\\
a    &= \dfrac {200} {4} \\\\
a    &= \dfrac {4 \times 50} {4} \\\\
a    &= \dfrac {\cancel {4} \times 50} { \cancel {4} } \\\\
a    &= 50 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of rectangle}            &= 70 \times 30 \\\\
                                    &= 2100 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Area of square}               &= a \times a \\\\
                                    &= 50 \times 50 \\\\
                                    &= 2500 \ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
\text{The difference between areas} &= 2500 - 2100 \\\\
                                    &= 400 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$400 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A square has a perimeter of $32 \ \text{cm}$. What is the area of the square?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A square has a perimeter of $32 \ \text{cm}$. What is the area of the square?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the length of the side of the square $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
4 \times a                       &= 32 \\\\
a                                &= \dfrac {32} {4} \\\\
a                                &= \dfrac {8 \times 4} {4} \\\\
a                                &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel {4}} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
a                                &= 8 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the area of the square.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area}                     &= 8 \times 8 \\\\
                                 &= 64 \ \text{cm} ^ 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$64 \ \text{cm} ^ 2$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

A rectangle has perimeter $32 \ \text{cm}$. The rectangle is three times as long as it is wide. What is the area of the rectangle?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A rectangle has perimeter $32 \ \text{cm}$. The rectangle is three times as long as it is wide. What is the area of the rectangle?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the width of the rectangle $= w$

Length of the rectangle $= 3w$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times (3w + w)                           &= 32 \\\\
2 \times 4w                                 &= 32 \\\\
8w                                          &= 32 \\\\
w                                           &= \dfrac {32} {8} \\\\
w                                           &= \dfrac {4 \times 8} {8} \\\\
w                                           &= \dfrac {4 \times \cancel {8}} {\cancel {8}} \\\\
w                                           &= 4 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Width}       &= 4 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Length}      &= 3 \times w \\\\
                    &= 3 \times 4 \\\\
                    &= 12 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the area of the square.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area}                                &= 12 \times 4 \\\\
                                            &= 48 \ \text{cm} ^ 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$48 \ \text{cm} ^ 2$

</div>

                                            &= 48 \ \text{cm} ^ 2
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The floor of a room is $3 \ \text{metres}$ wide and $4 \ \text{metres}$ long.
I am going to tile the floor with tiles that are $25 \ \text{centimetres}$ wide and $50 \ \text{centimetres}$ long.
How many tiles do I need to buy?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The floor of a room is $3 \ \text{metres}$ wide and $4 \ \text{metres}$ long.
I am going to tile the floor with tiles that are $25 \ \text{centimetres}$ wide and $50 \ \text{centimetres}$ long.
How many tiles do I need to buy?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The floor measurement is given in meters and tile measurement is in centimetres.

Let's convert all the measurements into meters.

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of tiles needed}  &= \dfrac {\text {Area of the floor}} {\text {Area of a tile}} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {4 \ \text{m} \times 3 \ \text{m}} {50 \ \text{cm} \times \ 25 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {4 \ \text{m} \times 3 \ \text{m}} {\dfrac {50} {100} \ \text{m} \times \dfrac {25} {100} \ \text{m}} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {12} {0.50 \times 0.25} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {12} {0.125} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {12 \times 1000} {0.125 \times 1000} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {12 \times 1000} {125} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {12 \times 125 \times 8} {125} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {12 \times \cancel {125} \times 8} {\cancel {125}} \\\\
                                &= 12 \times 8 \\\\
                                &= 96
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$96$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

How many carpet tiles, each $50 \ \text{cm} \times 50 \ \text{cm}$, would Kirin need to cover the floor?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many carpet tiles, each $50 \ \text{cm} \times 50 \ \text{cm}$, would Kirin need to cover the floor?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
_no_dot
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The floor measurement is given in $\text{meters}$ while the tile measurement is given in $\text{cm}$.

Let's convert the floor measurements into $\text{cm}$.

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of tiles}  &= \dfrac {\text{Area of the floor}} {\text{Area of a tile}} \\\\
                         &= \dfrac {50 \ \text{m}^2} {50 \ \text{cm} \times 50 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                         &= \dfrac {50 \times 10000 \ \text{cm}^2} {50 \ \text{cm} \times 50 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                         &= \dfrac {50 \times 10000} {50 \times 50} \\\\
                         &= \dfrac {50 \times 50 \times 200} {50 \times 50} \\\\
                         &= \dfrac {\cancel {50} \times \cancel {50} \times 200} {\cancel {50} \times \cancel {50}} \\\\
                         &= 200
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$200$

</div>
</div>

</code></pre>

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Perimeter of the worktop}    &= 2 (\text {length} + \text {width}) \\\\
                                    &= 2 (15 \times 20 \ \text{cm} + 6 \times 20 \ \text{cm}) \\\\
                                    &= 2 (15 \times \dfrac {20} {100} \ \text{m} + 6 \times \dfrac {20} {100} \ \text{m}) \\\\
                                    &= 2 (\dfrac {15 \times 20} {100} + \dfrac {6 \times 20} {100}) \\\\
                                    &= 2 (\dfrac {300} {100} + \dfrac {120} {100}) \\\\
                                    &= 2 (3 + 1.2) \\\\
                                    &= 2 \times 4.2 \\\\
                                    &= 8.4 \ \text{m}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

**Question**

Errol now uses a saw to cut the cube in two along the dotted line shown.

What fraction of the area of the two new blocks is not painted?

![papers/csse/2017/sample-paper-4/s01-q14-s03-i00.png](/assets/papers/csse/2017/sample-paper-4/s01-q14-s03-i00.png "papers/csse/2017/sample-paper-4/s01-q14-s03-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Errol now uses a saw to cut the cube in two along the dotted line shown.
<emptyline>
What fraction of the area of the two new blocks is not painted?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Surface area of cuboid} = 2 \times (\text{length} \times \text{width} + \text{width} \times \text {height} + \text {height} \times \text{length})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Fraction of the area not painted}    &= \dfrac {\text {Area of cube}} {\text {Area of block}} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {2400} {2 \times (20 \times 20 + 20 \times 10 + 10 \times 20)} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {2400} {2 \times (400 + 200 + 200)} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {2400} {2 \times 800} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {3 \times 800} {2 \times 800} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {3 \times \text \cancel {800}} {2 \times \text \cancel {800}} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {3} {2}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\dfrac {3} {2}$

</div>
</div>

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Perimeter}           &= 2 \times (5 + 3) \\\\
                            &= 2 \times 8 \\\\
                            &= 16 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Area}                &= 5 \times 3 \\\\
                            &= 15 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the width of the rectangle $= w$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
14 \times w                 &= 42 \\\\
14w                         &= 42 \\\\
w                           &= \dfrac {42} {14} \\\\
w                           &= \dfrac {14 \times 3} {14} \\\\
w                           &= \dfrac {\cancel {14} \times 3} {\cancel {14}} \\\\
w                           &= 3 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Width}               &= 3 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Perimeter}           &= 2 \times (14 + 3) \\\\
                            &= 2 \times 17 \\\\
                            &= 34 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$16 \ \text{cm}, 15 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A square has the same area as the rectangle below. What is the length of its side?

![papers/devonport-high-school-for-boys/2018/sample-paper-3/s01-q14-i00.png](/assets/papers/devonport-high-school-for-boys/2018/sample-paper-3/s01-q14-i00.png "papers/devonport-high-school-for-boys/2018/sample-paper-3/s01-q14-i00.png")

</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A square has the same area as the rectangle below. What is the length of its side?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of square $= s$

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of rectangle}      &= 6 \times 24 \\\\
                               &= 144 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of square} &= \text{Area of rectangle} \\\\
s \times s            &= 144 \\\\
s ^ 2                 &= 144 \\\\
s                     &= \sqrt {144} \\\\
s                     &= 12 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Length of the side of the square is $12 \ \text{cm}$.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$12 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">George cuts the rectangle up into an exact number of right-angled triangles, each with sides as shown in the diagram below.

<emptyline>
Calculate the number of triangles that he cuts from the rectangle.
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">

<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of triangle}        &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 12 \times 5 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 60 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {60} {2} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {30 \times 2} {2} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {30 \times \cancel {2}} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
                                &= 30 \ \text {mm} ^2
\end{aligned}
$

Let's calculate the no. of triangles that he cuts from the rectangle.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Total no. of triangles}                  &= \dfrac {\text {Area of rectangle}} {\text {Area of triangle}} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {1200} {30} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {40 \times 30} {30} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {40 \times \cancel {30}} {\cancel {30}} \\\\
                                                &= 40
\end{aligned}
$

No. of triangles George cuts $= 40$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$40$

\end{aligned}
