<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Louis hires a builder to lay the path. The builder charges $\pounds 8$ per hour basic labour for the job, and then $\pounds 1.50$ per slab he lays.

If he takes $3 \dfrac{1}{2}$ hours to finish the job, work out his overall fee.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Louis hires a builder to lay the path. The builder charges $\pounds 8$ per hour basic labour for the job, and then $\pounds 1.50$ per slab he lays.
<emptyline>
If he takes $3 \dfrac{1}{2}$ hours to finish the job, work out his overall fee.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Overall fee}  &= 8 \times (3 \dfrac{1} {2}) + 1.50 \times 40 \\\\
                    &= 8 \times \dfrac{7} {2} + 60 \\\\ 
                    &= \dfrac {4 \times 2 \times 7} {2} +60 \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {4 \times \cancel 2 \times 7} {\cancel 2} + 60 \\\\
                    &= 28 + 60 \\\\
                    &= \pounds 88
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 88$

</div>
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Perimeter of the area where bushes has to be planted}  &= 2 \times (12 \ \text{m} - 2 \ \text{m}- (25 \times 2)\ \text{cm} + 8 \ \text{m}- 2 \ \text{m} - (25 \times 2)\ \text{cm})  \\\\
                                                             &= 2 \times (12 \ \text{m} - 2 \ \text{m}- \dfrac {50} {100} \ \text{m} + 8 \ \text{m} - 2 \ \text{m}- \dfrac {50} {100}\ \text{m}) \\\\
                                                             &= 2 \times (12 - 2 + 8 - 2 - 1) \\\\
                                                             &= 2 \times (10 + 6 - 1) \\\\
                                                             &= 2 \times 15 \\\\
                                                             &= 30 \ \text{m} \\\\
\text{Total bushes that has to be planted}                   &= \dfrac {30 \ \text{m}} {50 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                                                             &= \dfrac {30 \times 100 \ \text{cm}} {50 \ \text{cm}} \\\\ 
                                                             &= \dfrac {30 \times 100} {50} \\\\
                                                             &= \dfrac {30 \times 50 \times 2} {50} \\\\
                                                             &= \dfrac {30 \times \cancel {50} \times 2} {\cancel {50}} \\\\
                                                             &= 60                                                        
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {\text{Area of the triangle}} {\text{Area of the next bigger triangle} }    &= \dfrac{1} {4} \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

Using this,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of the smallest triangle}     &= 1\ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
\text{Area of the next big triangle}     &= 4 \times 1 \\\\
                                         &= 4 \ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
\text{Area of the next bigger triangle}  &= 4 \times 4 \\\\
                                         &= 16 \ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
\text{Area of the biggest triangle}      &= 4 \times 16 \\\\
                                         &= 64 \ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

height $= 3 \text{cm}$

$

2 \times (l + w)   &= 18 \\\\

3 + w              &= \dfrac {18} {2} \\\\
3 + w              &= \dfrac {9 \times 2} {2} \\\\
3 + w              &= \dfrac {9 \times \cancel 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
3 + w              &= 9 \\\\
w                  &= 9 - 3 \\\\
w                  &= 6 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

\end{aligned}

As per the diagram, the shape can be divided into two rectangles

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of the shape}       &= \text {Rectangle 1} + \text {Rectangle 2} \\\\
                                &= 5 \times 10 + 4 \times 4 \\\\
                                &= 50 + 16 \\\\
                                &= 66 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}

Let's calculate the expressions given in the option and check which one matches the calculated area.

$
\begin{aligned}
10 \times 6 + 5 \times 4 \\\\
= 60 + 20 \\\\
= 80 \\\\
10 \times 5 + 9 \times 6 \\\\
= 50 + 54 \\\\
= 104 \\\\
9 \times 10 - 6 \times 4 \\\\
= 90 - 24 \\\\
= 66
\end{aligned}
$

Calculation C is correct for the area of the shape.

A swimming pool has a length that is four times of its width.

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A cube has six faces.

Theo builds a bigger cube out of $27$ little cubes.

He paints the outside of the big cube and lets the paint dry.

He then breaks it up into the original $27$ cubes.

What is the total number of **unpainted** faces on the little cubes? Show clearly how you get your answer. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A cube has six faces.
<emptyline>
Theo builds a bigger cube out of $27$ little cubes.
<emptyline>
He paints the outside of the big cube and lets the paint dry.
<emptyline>
He then breaks it up into the original $27$ cubes.
<emptyline>
What is the total number of **unpainted** faces on the little cubes? Show clearly how you get your answer. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">

</div>
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Total number of faces}            &= 27 \times 6 \\\\
                                        &= 162 \\\\
\text{Total number of faces painted}    &= (3 \times 3) \times 6 \\\\
                                        &= 9 \times 6 \\\\
                                        &= 54 
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Total number of faces not painted}    &= \text{Total number of faces} - \text{Total number of faces painted} \\\\
                                            &= 162 - 54 \\\\
                                            &= 108 
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$108$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Armand is buying grass seed for his garden.

The lawn he wishes to make is this shape.

![papers/forest-school/sample/sample-paper-2/s01-q21-i00.png](/assets/papers/forest-school/sample/sample-paper-2/s01-q21-i00.png "papers/forest-school/sample/sample-paper-2/s01-q21-i00.png")

Grass seed is sold by the bag. Each bag cost $\pounds 10$ and covers $3 \ \text{m} ^ {2}$.
How much will it cost him?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Armand is buying grass seed for his garden.
<emptyline>
The lawn he wishes to make is this shape.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
Grass seed is sold by the bag. Each bag cost $\pounds 10$ and covers $3 \ \text{m} ^ {2}$.
How much will it cost him?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

*ABBR: TODO:: Add drawing starts.*

{/* ![missing image](/papers/missing_image.svg) */}
TODOIMAGE


*TODO:: Show the diagram divided in two rectangles with the calculations for the parts which do not have measurements shown.
Show the length of the first rectangle $6 (10 - 4) \ \text{m}$ and width of the second rectangle $6 (20 - 10) \ \text{m}$.*

*ABBR: TODO:: Add drawing ends.*


As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of garden}                   &= \text{Rectangle 1} + \text{Rectangle 2} \\\\
                                        &= 6 \times 20 + 4 \times 10 \\\\
                                        &= 120 + 40 \\\\
                                        &= 160 \ \text{m}^2 \\\\
\text {Number of bags required}         &= \dfrac {\text {Area of the garden}} {\text {Area covered by one bag}} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {160} {3} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {160} {3} \\\\
                                        &= 54 \\\\
\text{Total cost}                       &= \text {Cost per bag} \times \text {Number of bags} \\\\
                                        &= \pounds 10 \times 54 \\\\
                                        &= \pounds 540
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 540$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Krishani draws a rectangle with area $12 \ \text{cm} ^ {2}$ and its sides are whole number lengths. Its perimeter is $14  \ \text{cm}$. 

How long is the longest side?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Krishani draws a rectangle with area $12 \ \text{cm} ^ {2}$ and its sides are whole number lengths. Its perimeter is $14  \ \text{cm}$. 
<emptyline>
How long is the longest side?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
l \times b               &= 12 \\\\
2 \times (l + b)         &= 14 \\\\
l + b                    &= \dfrac {14} {2} \\\\
l + b                    &= \dfrac {7 \times 2} {2} \\\\
l + b                    &= \dfrac {7 \times \cancel 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
l + b                    &= 7
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

- The product of the $2$ numbers is $12$. 
- The sum of the $2$ numbers is $7$.

Factors of $12 = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12$

Factor pairs of $20 = (1, 12), (2, 6), (3, 4)$

Using the factor pairs we will infer the values of p and q

| Factors   |        Sum          |           Product         |
|:-------:  |:-------------------:|:----------------------:   |
| $1, 12$   |       $13$          |       $12$                |
| $2, 6$    |       $8$           |       $12$                |
| $3, 4$    |       $7$           |       $12$                |

A quick check shows $3$ and  $4$ meets all the criteria above

Length of longest side $= 4$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Shape $A$ and shape $B$ are each made from five identical squares. The perimeter of shape $A$ is 
$72 \ \text{cm}$. Work out the perimeter of shape $B$. 

![papers/halifax-grammar-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q02-i00.png](/assets/papers/halifax-grammar-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q02-i00.png "papers/halifax-grammar-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q02-i00.png")

- $30 \ \text{cm}$
- $60 \ \text{cm}$
- $72 \ \text{cm}$
- $50 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Shape $A$ and shape $B$ are each made from five identical squares. The perimeter of shape $A$ is

</code></pre>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the length of a side of sqaure $= l$.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Perimeter of shape A}    &= 72 \ \text{cm} \\\\
12 \times l                     &= 72 \\\\
l                               &= \dfrac {72} {12} \\\\
l                               &= \dfrac {12 \times 6} {12} \\\\
l                               &= \dfrac {\cancel{12} \times 6} {\cancel{12}} \\\\
l                               &= 6 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{perimeter of figure B}    &= 10 \times l \\\\
                                &= 10 \times 6 \\\\
                                &= 60 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Answer**

$60 \ \text{cm}$

</div>

<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Perimeter}   &= \text {Sum of all sides} \\\\
                    &= 15 \ \text{cm} + 15 \ \text{cm} + 8 \ \text{cm} + 8 \ \text{cm} \\\\
                    &= 15 + 8 + 15 + 8 \\\\
                    &= 30 + 16 \\\\
                    &= 46 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Width of small rectangle}  &= \dfrac{(15 - 12)}{2} \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac{3} {2} \\\\
                                 &= 1.5 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Length of small rectangle} &= \dfrac{(8 - 4)}{2} \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac{4} {2} \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac{2 \times 2} {2} \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac{\cancel 2 \times 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                                 &= 2 
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area}                     &= \text {Area of big rectangle} - 4 \times \text {Area of corner rectangles} \\\\
                                 &= 15 \ \text{cm} \times 8 \ \text{cm} - 4 \times (1.5 \ \text{cm} \times 2 \ \text{cm}) \\\\
                                 &= 120 - 4 \times 3 \\\\
                                 &= 120 - 12 \\\\
                                 &= 108 \ \text{cm} ^ 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Perimeter $=$ $46 \ \text{cm}$

</div>

**Answer**

Area $=$ $108 \ \text{cm} ^ 2$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How much smaller is the area of a $60 \ \text{cm}$ by $40 \ \text{cm}$ rectangle than that of a square with the same perimeter? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How much smaller is the area of a $60 \ \text{cm}$ by $40 \ \text{cm}$ rectangle than that of a square with the same perimeter? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
4a         &= 2 \times (60 + 40) \\\\
4a         &= 2 \times 100 \\\\
4a         &= 200 \\\\
a          &= \dfrac {200} {4} \\\\
a          &= \dfrac {50 \times 4} {4} \\\\
a          &= \dfrac {50 \times \cancel {4} } {\cancel {4} }  \\\\
a          &= 50 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of square}            &= a \times a \\\\
                                 &= 50 \times 50 \\\\
                                 &= 2500 \ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
\text{Area of rectangle}         &= 60 \times 40 \\\\
                                 &= 2400 \ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
\text{Difference in thier areas} &= 2500 - 2400 \\\\
                                 &= 100 \ \text{cm}^2                             
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$100 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Gill's garden is $48 \ \text{m}$ long and $10 \ \text{m}$ wide 
and she wants to cover it with peat which comes in $60 \ \text{kg}$ sacks. 
$10 \ \text{kg}$ of peat covers an area of $20 \ \text{m}^2$. 

Work out the area of the garden:

How many sacks of peat does Gill need for the whole garden?

![papers/james-allens-girls-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q10-i00.png](/assets/papers/james-allens-girls-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q10-i00.png "papers/james-allens-girls-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q10-i00.png")  

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Gill's garden is $48 \ \text{m}$ long and $10 \ \text{m}$ wide 
and she wants to cover it with peat which comes in $60 \ \text{kg}$ sacks. 
$10 \ \text{kg}$ of peat covers an area of $20 \ \text{m}^2$. 
<emptyline>
Work out the area of the garden:
<emptyline>
How many sacks of peat does Gill need for the whole garden?
<emptyline>
%image%  
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of garden}                   &= 48 \times 10 \\\\
                                        &= 480 \ \text{m}^2 \\\\
\text {Number of sacks required}        &= \dfrac {\text {Area of the garden}} {\text {Area covered by 60 kg sack}} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {\text {Area of the garden}} {6 \times \text {Area covered by 10 kg peat}} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {480} {6 \times 2} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {12 \times 40} {12} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {\cancel {12} \times 40} {\cancel {12}} \\\\
                                        &= 40
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$40$

</div>
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="workings">

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

As per the diagram, the shape can be divided into three rectangles

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Total Area}           &= \text {Rectangle 1} + \text {Rectangle 2} + {Rectangle 3} \\\\
                             &= 3 \times 8 + 1 \times 3 + 6 \times 2 \\\\
                             &= 24 + 3 + 12 \\\\
                             &= 39 \ \text{cm} ^ 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

</div>

                             &= 36 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

\text {Are of the shape}        &= \text {Area of the rectangular piece} - 4 \times \text {Area of square} \\\\
                                &= 15 \times 21 - 4 \times (4 \times 4) \\\\
                                &= 315 - 64 \\\\
                                &= 251 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                                        &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 3 \times 8} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
                                        &= 3 \times 8 \\\\
                                        &= 24 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="workings">

<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

*ABBR: TODO:: Add drawing starts.*

{/* ![missing image](/papers/missing_image.svg) */}
TODOIMAGE


*TODO:: Show th diagram divided into a rectangle and triangle along with the measurements.*

*ABBR: TODO:: Add drawing ends.*


As per the diagram, the shape can be divided into a rectangle and a triangle

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Total Area}           &= \text {Rectangle} + \text {Triangle} \\\\
                             &= 8 \times 10 + \dfrac {1} {2} \times 8 \times 6 \\\\
                             &= 80 + \dfrac {8 \times 6} {2} \\\\
                             &= 80 + \dfrac {2 \times 4 \times 6} {2} \\\\
                             &= 80 + \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 4 \times 6} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
                             &= 80 + 4 \times 6 \\\\
                             &= 80 + 24 \\\\
                             &= 104 \ \text{cm} ^ 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$104 \ \text{cm} ^ 2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

For surface area of both cuboid , count the number of squares for each of them.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of squares in cuboid A}  &= 2 \times (4 \times 3) + 4 \times 4 \\\\
                                      &= 24 + 16 \\\\
                                      &= 40 \\\\
\text{Number of squares in cuboid B}  &= 4 \times (2 \times 3) + 2 \times (2 \times 2) \\\\
                                      &= 24 + 8 \\\\
                                      &= 32 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

They don't have same surface area.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

whose perimeter is $48 \ \text{cm}$ and whose width is one half of its length?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">whose perimeter is $48 \ \text{cm}$ and whose width is one half of its length?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the length of rectangle $= a$

Width $= \dfrac {1} {2} \times a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times (a + \dfrac {1} {2} \times a)                                  &= 48 \\\\
2 \times (a + \dfrac {a} {2})                                           &= 48 \\\\
2 \times (\dfrac {a \times 2} {1 \times 2} + \dfrac {a} {2})            &= 48 \\\\
2 \times (\dfrac {2a} {2} + \dfrac {a} {2})                             &= 48 \\\\
2 \times \dfrac {2a + a} {2}                                            &= 48 \\\\
\dfrac {2 \times (3 a)} {2}                                             &= 48 \\\\
\dfrac {\cancel {2} \times (3 a)} {\cancel {2}}                         &= 48 \\\\
3a                                                                      &= 48 \\\\
a                                                                       &= \dfrac {48} {3} \\\\
a                                                                       &= \dfrac {16 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a                                                                       &= \dfrac {16 \times \cancel {3}} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                                                                       &= 16 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Length $= 16 \ \text{cm}$

Width $= 8 \ \text{cm}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$16 \ \text{cm}, 8 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">whose area is $48 \ \text{cm}^2$, perimeter is $32 \ \text{cm}$ and length is greater than width?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the length of the rectangle $= l$
Let the width of the rectangle $= w$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
l \times w                                                      &= 48 \\\\
w                                                               &= \dfrac {48} {l} \\\\
2 \times (l + w)                                                &= 32 \\\\
2 \times (l + \dfrac {48} {l})                                  &= 32 \\\\
2 \times (\dfrac {l \times l} {1 \times l} + \dfrac {48} {l})   &= 32 \\\\
2 \times (\dfrac {l^2 + 48} {l})                                &= 32 \\\\
\dfrac {l^2 + 48} {l}                                           &= \dfrac {32} {2} \\\\
\dfrac {l^2 + 48} {l}                                           &= \dfrac {2 \times 16} {2} \\\\
\dfrac {l^2 + 48} {l}                                           &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 16} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
\dfrac {l^2 + 48} {l}                                           &= 16
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

whose area is $72 \ \text{cm}^2$, and width is twice its length?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">whose area is $72 \ \text{cm}^2$, and width is twice its length?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the length of rectangle $=a$

As per the question,

Width $= 2 \times a$

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times 2a  &= 72 \\\\
2 a^2        &= 72 \\\\
a^2          &= \dfrac {72} {2} \\\\
a^2          &= \dfrac {36 \times 2} {2} \\\\
a^2          &= \dfrac {36 \times \cancel {2}} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
a^2          &= 36 \\\\
a            &= \sqrt {36} \\\\
a            &= 6 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Length $=6 \ \text{ cm}$

Width $=12 \ \text{ cm}$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$6 \ \text{cm}, \ 12 \ \text{cm}$

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is the total surface area of all $6$ sides?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the total surface area of all $6$ sides?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Surface area of cuboid} = 2 \times (\text{length} \times \text{width} + \text{width} \times \text {height} + \text {height} \times \text{length})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Total surface area} &= 2 \times (8 \times 5 + 8 \times 6 + 6 \times 5) \\\\
                           &= 2 \times (40 + 48 + 30) \\\\
                           &= 2 \times 118 \\\\
                           &= 236 \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$236 \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

If the area of the front face doubles but the $8 \ \text{cm}$ width does not change what must the new height be?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If the area of the front face doubles but the $8 \ \text{cm}$ width does not change what must the new height be?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the new height $= h$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
h \times 8      &= 2 \times (6 \times 8) \\\\
8h              &= 2 \times 6 \times 8 \\\\
h               &= \dfrac {2 \times 6 \times 8} {8} \\\\
h               &= \dfrac {2 \times 6 \times \cancel {8}} {\cancel {8}} \\\\
h               &= 2 \times 6 \\\\
h               &= 12 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

The new height is $12 \ \text{cm}$.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$12 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A rectangle has a length of $50 \ \text{mm}$ and has the same area as a square with side $70 \ \text{mm}$.

Calculate the perimeter of the rectangle.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A rectangle has a length of $50 \ \text{mm}$ and has the same area as a square with side $70 \ \text{mm}$.
<emptyline>
Calculate the perimeter of the rectangle.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let width of the rectangle $= w$

Let side of the square $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
50 \times w             &= 70 \times 70 \\\\
50 \times w             &= 4900 \\\\
w                       &= \dfrac {4900} {50} \\\\
w                       &= \dfrac {50 \times 98} {50} \\\\
w                       &= \dfrac {\cancel {50} \times 98} {\cancel {50}} \\\\
w                       &= 98 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the perimeter of the rectangle.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Perimeter}           &= 2 \times (50 + 98) \\\\
                            &= 2 \times 148 \\\\
                            &= 296 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$296 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The area of the small shaded square is $1\ \text{square centimetre}$.

What is the area of the larger shaded square?

![papers/north-london-collegiate-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q17-i00.png](/assets/papers/north-london-collegiate-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q17-i00.png "papers/north-london-collegiate-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q17-i00.png")

In the grid below, draw a square with an area of $2\;cm^2$.

![papers/north-london-collegiate-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q17-i01.png](/assets/papers/north-london-collegiate-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q17-i01.png "papers/north-london-collegiate-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q17-i01.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The area of the small shaded square is $1\ \text{square centimetre}$.
<emptyline>
What is the area of the larger shaded square?
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
In the grid below, draw a square with an area of $2\;cm^2$.
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Number of full squares in larger shaded area $= 4$ 

Number of half squares in larger shaded area $= 8$

Area of half square  $= \dfrac{1} {2} \ \text{cm}^2 $ 

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area}  &= 4 \times 1 \ \text{cm}^2 + 8 \times \dfrac{1} {2} \ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
             &= 4 + \dfrac {8} {2} \\\\
             &= 4 + \dfrac {4 \times 2} {2} \\\\
             &= 4 + \dfrac {4 \times \cancel 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
             &= 4 + 4 \\\\
             &= 8\ \text{cm}^2 
\end{aligned}
$

$8\ \text{cm}^2$

</div>

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of Tiles}     &= \dfrac {\text {Area of shape}} {\text {Area of a tile}} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {\dfrac {12 + 4} {2} \times 4} {\dfrac {1} {2} \times 4 \times 4} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {\dfrac {16} {2} \times 4} {\dfrac {4 \times 4} {2}} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {16 \times 4 \times 2} {4 \times 4 \times 2} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {4 \times 4 \times 4 \times 2} {4 \times 4 \times 2} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {4 \times \cancel {4} \times \cancel {4} \times \cancel {2}} {\cancel {4} \times \cancel {4} \times \cancel {2}} \\\\
                            &= 4
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                            &= \dfrac {\dfrac {4 \times 4} {2} + 8 \times 4 + 8 \times 4} {\dfrac {4 \times 4} {2}} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {\dfrac {2 \times 2 \times 4} {2} + 8 \times 4 + 8 \times 4} {\dfrac {2 \times 2 \times 4} {2}} \\\\

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A piece of wire $36 \ \text{cm}$ long is bent into the shape of a rectangle. If the rectangle is twice as long as it is wide, what is the area?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A piece of wire $36 \ \text{cm}$ long is bent into the shape of a rectangle. If the rectangle is twice as long as it is wide, what is the area?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the width of the rectangle $= w$

Length of the rectangle $= 2w$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times (w + 2w)           &= 36 \\\\
2 \times 3w                 &= 36 \\\\
6w                          &= 36 \\\\
w                           &= \dfrac {36} {6} \\\\
w                           &= \dfrac {6 \times 6} {6} \\\\
w                           &= \dfrac {\cancel {6} \times 6} {\cancel {6}} \\\\
w                           &= 6 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Width}               &= 6 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Length}              &= 2 \times 6 \\\\
                            &= 12 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the area of the rectangle.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area}            &= 6 \times 12 \\\\
                        &= 72 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$72 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

![papers/oundle-school/2008/sample-paper-1/s01-q18-i00.png](/assets/papers/oundle-school/2008/sample-paper-1/s01-q18-i00.png "papers/oundle-school/2008/sample-paper-1/s01-q18-i00.png")

A piece of wire $36 \ \text{cm}$ long is bent into the shape of a rectangle. If the rectangle is twice as long as it is wide, what is its area (in square centimetres)?

![papers/oundle-school/2008/sample-paper-1/s01-q18-i01.png](/assets/papers/oundle-school/2008/sample-paper-1/s01-q18-i01.png "papers/oundle-school/2008/sample-paper-1/s01-q18-i01.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%image%
<emptyline>
A piece of wire $36 \ \text{cm}$ long is bent into the shape of a rectangle. If the rectangle is twice as long as it is wide, what is its area (in square centimetres)?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$

- ABBR: $\text{Area} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times (l + b)         &= 36 \\\\
l + b                    &= 18 \\\\
2b + b                   &= 18 \\\\
3b                       &= 18 \\\\
b                        &= 6 \\\\
l                        &= 2b \\\\
l                        &= 2 \times 6 \\\\
l                        &= 12 \\\\
\text{Area}              &= l \times b \\\\
\text{Area}              &= 12 \times 6 \\\\
\text{Area}              &= 72
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$72$

</div>
</div>

<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</code></pre>

<div class="formulacodeblock_title">

- rtq_abbr_formula_katex_area_rectangle
</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="workingcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Working Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times (l + b)         &= 36 \\\\
l + b                    &= 18 \\\\
2b + b                   &= 18 \\\\
3b                       &= 18 \\\\
b                        &= 6 \\\\
l                        &= 2b \\\\
l                        &= 2 \times 6 \\\\
l                        &= 12 \\\\
\text{Area}              &= l \times b \\\\
\text{Area}              &= 12 \times 6 \\\\
\text{Area}              &= 72
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The ratio of height to width on an old television screen is $3:4$.

If the height of a television screen was $21 \ \text{cm}$, find the perimeter of the screen.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The ratio of height to width on an old television screen is $3:4$.
<emptyline>
If the height of a television screen was $21 \ \text{cm}$, find the perimeter of the screen.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the width of the television $= w$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {21} {w}                                     &= \dfrac {3} {4} \\\\
21 \times 4                                         &= 3 \times w \\\\
3 \times w                                          &= 21 \times 4 \\\\
3w                                                  &= 21 \times 4 \\\\
w                                                   &= \dfrac {21 \times 4} {3} \\\\
w                                                   &= \dfrac {3 \times 7 \times 4} {3} \\\\
w                                                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {3} \times 7 \times 4} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
w                                                   &= 7 \times 4 \\\\
w                                                   &= 28 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Perimeter of television}                      &= 2 \times (21 + 28) \\\\
                                                    &= 2 \times 49 \\\\
                                                    &= 98 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$98 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

x                                            &= \dfrac {\cancel{2} \times 8} {\cancel{2}} \\\\
x                                            &= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>

![papers/royal-russell-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q23-i00.png](/assets/papers/royal-russell-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q23-i00.png "papers/royal-russell-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q23-i00.png")     ![papers/royal-russell-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q23-i01.png](/assets/papers/royal-russell-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q23-i01.png "papers/royal-russell-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q23-i01.png")    ![papers/royal-russell-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q23-i02.png](/assets/papers/royal-russell-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q23-i02.png "papers/royal-russell-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q23-i02.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Mrs Suzie needs to cover a floor measuring $3\ \text{m}$ by $2\ \text{m}$. There are three possible options:
<emptyline>
%image%     %image%    %image%
<emptyline>
Which option is the cheapest? Show all your workings & explain clearly. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
_no_dot
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The floor measurement is given in $\text{m}$ while the tile measurement is given in $\text{cm}$.

Let's convert the floor measurements into $\text{cm}$.

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of Acron tiles}       &= \dfrac {\text {Area of floor}} {\text {Area of a tile}} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {3 \ \text{m} \times 2 \ \text{m}} {50 \ \text{cm} \times 50 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {3 \times 100 \ \text{cm} \times 2 \times 100 \ \text{cm}} {50 \ \text{cm} \times 50 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {3 \times 100 \times 2 \times 100} {50 \times 50} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {3 \times 50 \times 2 \times 2 \times 50 \times 2} {50 \times 50} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {3 \times \cancel {50} \times 2 \times 2 \times \cancel {50} \times 2} {\cancel {50} \times \cancel {50}} \\\\
                                    &= 3 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \\\\
                                    &= 24 \\\\
\text {Total cost of Acron tiles}   &= 4 \times 24 \\\\
                                    &= \pounds \ 96
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of Beeching tiles}        &= \dfrac {\text {Area of floor}} {\text {Area of a tile}} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {3 \ \text{m} \times 2 \ \text{m}} {60 \ \text{cm} \times 40 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {3 \times 100 \ \text{cm} \times 2 \times 100 \ \text{cm}} {60 \ \text{cm} \times 40 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {3 \times 10 \times 10 \times 2 \times 4 \times 25} {3 \times 2 \times 10 \times 4 \times 10} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {\cancel {3} \times \cancel {10} \times \cancel {10} \times \cancel {2} \times \cancel {4} \times 25} {\cancel {3} \times \cancel {2} \times \cancel {10} \times \cancel {10} \times \cancel {4}} \\\\
                                        &= 25
\text {Total cost of Beeching tiles}    &= 3 \times 25 \\\\
                                        &= \pounds \ 75
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Total cost of carpet}            &= \text {Cost per square metre} \times \text {Area of floor} + \text {Fitting cost} \\\\
                                        &= 14 \times (3 \times 2) + 30 \\\\ 
                                        &= 14 \times 6 + 30 \\\\ 
                                        &= 84 + 30 \\\\ 
                                        &= \pounds \ 114
\end{aligned}
$

Beeching tiles are the cheapest.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Beeching tiles

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Six cubes each have a surface area of $24\ \text{cm}^2$. They are joined together to make a cuboid.

![papers/sevenoaks-school/2010/sample-paper-1/s01-q14-i00.png](/assets/papers/sevenoaks-school/2010/sample-paper-1/s01-q14-i00.png "papers/sevenoaks-school/2010/sample-paper-1/s01-q14-i00.png")

What could the surface area of this cuboid be? 

There are two different answers. Write them both.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Six cubes each have a surface area of $24\ \text{cm}^2$. They are joined together to make a cuboid.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
What could the surface area of this cuboid be? 
<emptyline>
There are two different answers. Write them both.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Surface area of cube} = 6 \times \text{edge} \times \text{edge}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
6a^2   &= 24 \\\\
a^2    &= \dfrac {24} {6} \\\\
a^2    &= \dfrac {6 \times 4} {6} \\\\
a^2    &= \dfrac {\cancel 6 \times 4} {\cancel 6} \\\\
a^2    &= 4 \\\\
a      &= \sqrt {4} \\\\
a      &= 2 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Possiblity $1 =$ $2$ cubes piled upon one another 

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Surface Area} &= 2 \times (3a \times 2a) + 2 \times 3a \times a + 2 \times a \times a \\\\
                    &= 12a^2 + 6a^2 + 2a^2 \\\\
                    &= 20a^2 \\\\
                    &= 20 \times 2 \times 2 \\\\
                    &= 80 \ \text{cm}^2 
\end{aligned}
$

Possiblity $2 =$ $1$ cubes piled upon one another 

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Surface Area} &= 4 \times (6a \times a) + 2 \times a \times a \\\\
                    &= 24a^2 + 2a^2 \\\\
                    &= 26a^2 \\\\
                    &= 26 \times 2 \times 2 \\\\
                    &= 104 \ \text{cm}^2 
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$80 \ \text{cm}^2 ,104 \ \text{cm}^2 $

</div>
</div>

**Question**

This design has one large square and two identical small squares.

![papers/sevenoaks-school/2011/sample-paper-2/s01-q12-i00.png](/assets/papers/sevenoaks-school/2011/sample-paper-2/s01-q12-i00.png "papers/sevenoaks-school/2011/sample-paper-2/s01-q12-i00.png")

Calculate the length of a side of the large square.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + b                   &= 28 \\\\

2a + b                  &= 36 \\\\
2a + (28 - a)           &= 36 \\\\
a + 28                  &= 36 \\\\
a                       &= 36 - 28 \\\\
a                       &= 8 \ \text{cm} \\\\
b                       &= 28 - a \\\\
                        &= 28 - 8 \\\\
                        &= 20 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Length of the side of the large square $= 20 \ \text{cm}$.

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Each square is one square unit. What is the area of the shaded triangle?

![papers/sevenoaks-school/2014/sample-paper-5/s01-q10-i00.png](/assets/papers/sevenoaks-school/2014/sample-paper-5/s01-q10-i00.png "papers/sevenoaks-school/2014/sample-paper-5/s01-q10-i00.png")

</div>

<emptyline>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

\text {Area of the shaded triangle}             &= 4 \times \text {Square} - \text {Triangle 1} - \text {Triangle 2} - \text {Triangle 3} \\\\
                                                &= 4 \times 1 \times 1 - \dfrac {1} {2} \times 1 \times 2 - \dfrac {1} {2} \times 1 \times 2 - \dfrac {1} {2} \times 1 \times 1 \\\\
                                                &= 4 - \dfrac {2 \times 1} {2} - \dfrac {2 \times 1} {2} - \dfrac {1} {2} \\\\

                                                &= 4 - 1 - 1 - \dfrac {1} {2} \\\\

\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

My vegetable patch is rectangular in shape and measures $200 \times 450 \ \text{centimetres}$. I have planted vegetables in $\dfrac {2} {3}$ of the patch. One half of that contains carrots. What area of the patch has been planted with carrots?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">My vegetable patch is rectangular in shape and measures $200 \times 450 \ \text{centimetres}$. I have planted vegetables in $\dfrac {2} {3}$ of the patch. One half of that contains carrots. What area of the patch has been planted with carrots?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of the patch with vegetables}       &= \dfrac {2} {3} \times \text {Area of whole patch} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {2} {3} \times \text 200 \times 450\\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {2 \times 200 \times 450} {3} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {2 \times 200 \times 3 \times 150} {3} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {2 \times 200 \times \cancel {3} \times 150} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
                                                &= 2 \times 200 \times 150 \\\\
                                                &= 60000 \ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
\text {Area of the patch with carrots}          &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times \text {Area of the patch with vegetables} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 60000 \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {60000} {2} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {2 \times 30000} {2} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 30000} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
                                                &= 30000 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$30000 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Which two shapes have the same area?

![papers/sevenoaks-school/2014/sample-paper-5/s01-q16-i00.png](/assets/papers/sevenoaks-school/2014/sample-paper-5/s01-q16-i00.png "papers/sevenoaks-school/2014/sample-paper-5/s01-q16-i00.png")

This may be helpful:

![papers/sevenoaks-school/2014/sample-paper-5/s01-q16-i01.png](/assets/papers/sevenoaks-school/2014/sample-paper-5/s01-q16-i01.png "papers/sevenoaks-school/2014/sample-paper-5/s01-q16-i01.png")

$\text{Area of a trapezium} = \dfrac {1} {2} (a + b) h$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Which two shapes have the same area?
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
This may be helpful:
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
$\text{Area of a trapezium} = \dfrac {1} {2} (a + b) h$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of trapezium} = \dfrac {\text{length} + \text{width}} {2} \times \text {height}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the height be $=h$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of A} &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 80 \times h \\\\
                 &= \dfrac {80h} {2} \\\\
                 &= \dfrac {40h \times 2} {2} \\\\
                 &= \dfrac {40h \times \cancel 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                 &= 40h \\\\
\text{Area of B} &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 160 \times h \\\\
                 &= \dfrac {160h} {2} \\\\
                 &= \dfrac {80h \times 2} {2} \\\\
                 &= \dfrac {80h \times \cancel 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                 &= 80h \\\\
\text{Area of C} &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times (60 + 100) \times h \\\\
                 &= \dfrac {160h} {2} \\\\
                 &= \dfrac {80h \times 2} {2} \\\\
                 &= \dfrac {80h \times \cancel 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                 &= 80h \\\\
\text{Area of D} &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 180 \times h \\\\
                 &= \dfrac {180h} {2} \\\\
                 &= \dfrac {90h \times 2} {2} \\\\
                 &= \dfrac {90h \times \cancel 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                 &= 90h \\\\
\text{Area of E} &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times (170 + 30) \times h \\\\
                 &= \dfrac {200h} {2} \\\\
                 &= \dfrac {100h \times 2} {2} \\\\
                 &= \dfrac {100h \times \cancel 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                 &= 100h \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

Shape B and C have same shape.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

B and C

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A floor measures $5 \ \text{m}$ by $4 \ \text{m}$. It is to be covered by rectangular tiles measuring $80 \ \text{cm}$ by $50 \ \text{cm}$. How many tiles are needed?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A floor measures $5 \ \text{m}$ by $4 \ \text{m}$. It is to be covered by rectangular tiles measuring $80 \ \text{cm}$ by $50 \ \text{cm}$. How many tiles are needed?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The floor measurement is given in meters and tile measurement is in centimetres.

Let's convert the floor measurements into $\text{cm}$.

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of tiles}             &= \dfrac {\text{Area of floor}} {\text{Area of a tile}} \\\\
                                   &= \dfrac {5 \ \text{m} \times 4 \ \text{m}} {80 \ \text{cm} \times 50 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                                   &= \dfrac {5 \times 100 \ \text{cm} \times 4 \times 100 \ \text{cm}} {80 \ \text{cm} \times 50 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                                   &= \dfrac {5 \times 100 \times 4 \times 100} {80 \times 50} \\\\
                                   &= \dfrac {200000} {4000} \\\\
                                   &= \dfrac {50 \times 4000} {4000} \\\\
                                   &= \dfrac {50 \times \cancel {4000}} {\cancel {4000}} \\\\
                                   &= 50
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$50$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="formulacodeblock_title">

</div>

</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="workingcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Working Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The floor measurement is given in meters and tile measurement is in centimetres.
<emptyline>
Let's convert the floor measurements into $\text{cm}$.
<emptyline>
As per the question,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of tiles}             &= \dfrac {\text{Area of floor}} {\text{Area of a tile}} \\\\
                                   &= \dfrac {5 \ \text{m} \times 4 \ \text{m}} {80 \ \text{cm} \times 50 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                                   &= \dfrac {5 \times 100 \ \text{cm} \times 4 \times 100 \ \text{cm}} {80 \ \text{cm} \times 50 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                                   &= \dfrac {5 \times 100 \times 4 \times 100} {80 \times 50} \\\\
                                   &= \dfrac {200000} {4000} \\\\
                                   &= \dfrac {50 \times 4000} {4000} \\\\
                                   &= \dfrac {50 \times \cancel {4000}} {\cancel {4000}} \\\\
                                   &= 50
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answercodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="answercodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Option Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%empty%</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="answercodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="answercodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="answercodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Answer Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$50$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A square has a perimeter of $5.6 \ \text{m}$. Calculate the area of the square.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A square has a perimeter of $5.6 \ \text{m}$. Calculate the area of the square.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of the square $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
4 \times a                        &= 5.6 \\\\
a                                 &= \dfrac {5.6} {4} \\\\
a                                 &= \dfrac {1.4 \times 4} {4} \\\\
a                                 &= \dfrac {1.4 \times \cancel{4}} {\cancel{4}} \\\\
a                                 &= 1.4 \ \text{m}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's calculate the area of square.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area}                        &= 1.4 \times 1.4 \\\\
                                    &= 1.96 \ \text{m}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$1.96 \ \text{m}^2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find the area of the shaded region in the diagram below. Give your answer in terms of $\pi$.

![papers/sevenoaks-school/2016/sample-paper-7/s01-q16-i00.png](/assets/papers/sevenoaks-school/2016/sample-paper-7/s01-q16-i00.png "papers/sevenoaks-school/2016/sample-paper-7/s01-q16-i00.png")

Diagram not drawn to scale.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find the area of the shaded region in the diagram below. Give your answer in terms of $\pi$.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
Diagram not drawn to scale.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of circle} = \pi \times \text{radius} \times \text{radius}$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of semi-circle} = \dfrac {1} {2} \times \pi \times \text{radius} \times \text{radius}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of the shaded region}       &= \text {Area of bigger semi-circle} - \text {Area of smaller circle} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times \pi \times 5 \times 5 - \pi \times \dfrac {5} {2} \times \dfrac {5} {2} \\\\ 
                                        &= \dfrac {\pi \times 5 \times 5} {2} - \dfrac {\pi \times 5 \times 5} {2 \times 2} \\\\ 
                                        &= \dfrac {\pi \times 5 \times 5} {2} - \dfrac {\pi \times 5 \times 5} {4} \\\\ 
                                        &= \dfrac {\pi \times 5 \times 5 \times 2} {2 \times 2} - \dfrac {\pi \times 5 \times 5} {4} \\\\ 
                                        &= \dfrac {50 \ \pi} {4} - \dfrac {25 \ \pi} {4} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {50 \ \pi - 25 \ \pi} {4} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {25} {4} \ \pi
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\dfrac {25} {4} \ \pi$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</code></pre>

<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">As per the diagram,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of the shaded region}       &= \text {Area of bigger semi-circle} - \text {Area of smaller circle} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times \pi \times 5 \times 5 - \pi \times \dfrac {5} {2} \times \dfrac {5} {2} \\\\ 
                                        &= \dfrac {\pi \times 5 \times 5} {2} - \dfrac {\pi \times 5 \times 5} {2 \times 2} \\\\ 
                                        &= \dfrac {\pi \times 5 \times 5} {2} - \dfrac {\pi \times 5 \times 5} {4} \\\\ 
                                        &= \dfrac {\pi \times 5 \times 5 \times 2} {2 \times 2} - \dfrac {\pi \times 5 \times 5} {4} \\\\ 
                                        &= \dfrac {50 \ \pi} {4} - \dfrac {25 \ \pi} {4} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {50 \ \pi - 25 \ \pi} {4} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {25} {4} \ \pi
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
