<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A square is divided into three congruent rectangles. The middle rectangle is removed and replaced on the side of the original square to form an octagon as shown. 

![papers/sevenoaks-school/2016/sample-paper-7/s01-q25-i00.png](/assets/papers/sevenoaks-school/2016/sample-paper-7/s01-q25-i00.png "papers/sevenoaks-school/2016/sample-paper-7/s01-q25-i00.png")

![papers/sevenoaks-school/2016/sample-paper-7/s01-q25-i01.png](/assets/papers/sevenoaks-school/2016/sample-paper-7/s01-q25-i01.png "papers/sevenoaks-school/2016/sample-paper-7/s01-q25-i01.png") 


What is the ratio of the perimeter of the square to the perimeter of the octagon?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A square is divided into three congruent rectangles. The middle rectangle is removed and replaced on the side of the original square to form an octagon as shown. 
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
%image% 
<emptyline>

What is the ratio of the perimeter of the square to the perimeter of the octagon?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of square $=a$

Side of the divided parts $= \dfrac{a} {3} $

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Perimeter of square}   &= 4a \\\\
\text{Perimeter of octagon}  &= a + a + 2 \times (a + \dfrac {a} {3}) + 2 \times (a - \dfrac {a} {3}) \\\\
                             &= 2a + 2a + \dfrac {2a} {3} + 2a - \dfrac {2a} {3} \\\\
                             &= 6a \\\\
\text{Fraction}              &= \dfrac {6a} {4a} \\\\
                             &= \dfrac {2 \times 3 \times a} {2 \times 2 \times a} \\\\
                             &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 3 \times \cancel a} {\cancel 2 \times 2 \times \cancel a} \\\\
                             &= \dfrac {3} {2}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\dfrac {3} {2}$

</div>
</div>

</code></pre>

<div class="workingcodeblock_title">

</div>

<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Perimeter of square}   &= 4a \\\\
\text{Perimeter of octagon}  &= a + a + 2 \times (a + \dfrac {a} {3}) + 2 \times (a - \dfrac {a} {3}) \\\\
                             &= 2a + 2a + \dfrac {2a} {3} + 2a - \dfrac {2a} {3} \\\\
                             &= 6a \\\\
\text{Fraction}              &= \dfrac {6a} {4a} \\\\
                             &= \dfrac {2 \times 3 \times a} {2 \times 2 \times a} \\\\
                             &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 3 \times \cancel a} {\cancel 2 \times 2 \times \cancel a} \\\\
                             &= \dfrac {3} {2}
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A piece of wire $42 \ \text{cm}$ long is bent into the shape of a rectangle. If the rectangle is twice as long as it is wide, what is its area?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A piece of wire $42 \ \text{cm}$ long is bent into the shape of a rectangle. If the rectangle is twice as long as it is wide, what is its area?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

Let the width of the rectangle $= w$

Length of the rectangle $= 2w$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times (2w + w)                          &= 42 \\\\
2 \times 3w                                &= 42 \\\\
6w                                         &= 42 \\\\
w                                          &= \dfrac {42} {6} \\\\
w                                          &= \dfrac {7 \times 6} {6} \\\\
w                                          &= \dfrac {7 \times \cancel {6}} {\cancel {6}} \\\\
w                                          &= 7 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the area of the rectangle.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area}                               &= (2 \times 7) \times 7 \\\\
                                           &= 14 \times 7 \\\\
                                           &= 98 \ \text{cm} ^ 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$98 \ \text{cm} ^ 2$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

![papers/sevenoaks-school/2019/sample-paper-10/s01-q11-i00.png](/assets/papers/sevenoaks-school/2019/sample-paper-10/s01-q11-i00.png "papers/sevenoaks-school/2019/sample-paper-10/s01-q11-i00.png")

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Dini has $72$ small wooden cubes, each measuring $1 \ \text{cm} \times 1 \ \text{cm} \times 1 \ \text{cm}$. She arranges them all so that they form a cuboid. Given that the perimeter of the base of the cuboid is $16 \ \text{cm}$, what is its height?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Dini has $72$ small wooden cubes, each measuring $1 \ \text{cm} \times 1 \ \text{cm} \times 1 \ \text{cm}$. She arranges them all so that they form a cuboid. Given that the perimeter of the base of the cuboid is $16 \ \text{cm}$, what is its height?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$

- ABBR: $\text{Volume of a cuboid} = \text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{height}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times (l + b) &= 16 \\\\
l + b            &= \dfrac {16} {2} \\\\
l + b            &= \dfrac {8 \times 2} {2} \\\\
l + b            &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
l + b            &= 8
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
l \times b \times h &= 72 \times 1 \times 1 \times 1 \\\\
l \times b \times h &= 72 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $3$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

- The product of the $3$ numbers is $72$. 
- The sum of the $2$ numbers is $8$.

Factors of $72 = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 72$

Factor pairs of $72 = (1, 12), (2, 6), (3, 4)$

Using the factor pairs we will infer the values of p and q

| Factors   |        Sum          |           Product         |
|:-------:  |:-------------------:|:----------------------:   |
| $1, 12$   |       $13$          |       $12$                |
| $2, 6$    |       $8$           |       $12$                |
| $3, 4$    |       $7$           |       $12$                |

A quick check shows $3$ and  $4$ meets all the criteria above

Length of longest side $= 4$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4$

</div>
</div>

- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}
4 \times a            &= 36\\\\
a                     &= \dfrac {36} {4} \\\\
a                     &= \dfrac {4 \times 9} {4} \\\\
a                     &= \dfrac {\cancel{4} \times 9} {\cancel{4}} \\\\
a                     &= 9 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the area of the square.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area}             &= 9 \times 9 \\\\
                        &= 81 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times (25 + l)                           &= 120 \\\\
25 + l                                      &= \dfrac {120} {2} \\\\
25 + l                                      &= \dfrac {60 \times 2} {2} \\\\
25 + l                                      &= \dfrac {60 \times \cancel {2}} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
25 + l                                      &= 60 \\\\
l                                           &= 60 - 25 \\\\
l                                           &= 35 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the area of the rectangle.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area}            &= 25 \times 35 \\\\
                        &= 875 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many $20 \ \text{cm}$ by $30 \ \text{cm}$ carpet tiles are needed to cover a $5 \ \text{m}$ by $6 \ \text{m}$ rectangular floor? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many $20 \ \text{cm}$ by $30 \ \text{cm}$ carpet tiles are needed to cover a $5 \ \text{m}$ by $6 \ \text{m}$ rectangular floor? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The Floor measurement is given in metres while the tile measurement is given in cm.

Let's convert the wall measurements into $\text{cm}$.

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of tiles}  &= \dfrac {\text{Area of the Wall}} {\text{Area of a Tile}} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {5 \ \text{m} \times 6 \ \text{m} } { 20 \ \text{cm} \times 30 \ \text{cm} } \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {5 \times 100  \ \text{cm} \times 6 \times 100 \ \text{cm} } { 20 \ \text{cm} \times 30 \ \text{cm} } \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {5 \times 100 \times 6 \times 100 } { 20  \times 30 } \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {3000} {60} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {60 \times 500} {60} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {\cancel {60} \times 500} {\cancel {60}} \\\\
                        &= 500
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$500$

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find the width of one cube, in $\text{cm}$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find the width of one cube, in $\text{cm}$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Volume of a cube} = (\text{Side}) ^ { 3 }$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the width of one cube $= w$

As per the question,

Number of cubes $= 7$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Total Volume}            &= 56 \\\\
7 \times w^3                    &= 56 \\\\
7w^3                            &= 56 \\\\
w^3                             &= \dfrac {56} {7} \\\\
w^3                             &= \dfrac {7 \times 8} {7} \\\\
w^3                             &= \dfrac {\cancel {7} \times 8} {\cancel {7}} \\\\
w^3                             &= 8 \\\\
w                               &= \sqrt[3] {8} \\\\
w                               &= 2 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Width of one cube is $2 \ \text{cm}$.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$2 \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

Sarah only has $24 \ \text{litres}$ of water. How deep can she fill the tank? (Each litre of water occupies $1000 \ \text{cm}^3$)

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Sarah only has $24 \ \text{litres}$ of water. How deep can she fill the tank? (Each litre of water occupies $1000 \ \text{cm}^3$)
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
_no_dot
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Volume of a cuboid} = \text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{height}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The height measurement of filled tank will be in $\text{cm}$ while the volume measurement is given in $\text{litre}$.

Let's convert the volume measurements into $\text{cm}$.

Let the height to which water can be filled (in cm) $= h$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
60 \ \text{cm} \times 20 \ \text{cm} \times h \ \text{cm}    &= 24 \ \text{litres} \\\\
60 \ \text{cm} \times 20 \ \text{cm} \times h \ \text{cm}    &= 24 \times 1000 \ \text{cm}^3 \\\\
60 \times 20 \times h                                           &= 24 \times 1000 \\\\
1200 \times h                                                   &= 24000 \\\\
h                                                               &= \dfrac {24000} {1200} \\\\
h                                                               &= \dfrac {1200 \times 20} {1200} \\\\
h                                                               &= \dfrac {\cancel {1200} \times 20} {\cancel {1200}} \\\\
h                                                               &= 20 \ \text{cm} 
\end{aligned}
$

Sarah can fill the tank upto $20 \ \text{cm}$.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$20 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

                            &=  9 \ \text{m}^2
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The diagram shows a shaded triangle inside a larger triangle: 

![papers/st-pauls-girls-school/2016/sample-paper-1/s01-q18-i00.png](/assets/papers/st-pauls-girls-school/2016/sample-paper-1/s01-q18-i00.png "papers/st-pauls-girls-school/2016/sample-paper-1/s01-q18-i00.png")

The area of the shaded triangle is $52 \ \text{cm}^2$. 

The area of the shaded triangle is $\dfrac{4}{9}$ of the area of the larger triangle.

Calculate the area of the larger triangle.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The diagram shows a shaded triangle inside a larger triangle: 
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
The area of the shaded triangle is $52 \ \text{cm}^2$. 
<emptyline>
The area of the shaded triangle is $\dfrac{4}{9}$ of the area of the larger triangle.
<emptyline>
Calculate the area of the larger triangle.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of shaded triangle}     &= \dfrac {4} {9} \times \text {Area of larger triangle} \\\\
\text {Area of larger triangle}     &= \dfrac {9} {4} \times \text {Area of shaded triangle} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {9} {4} \times 52 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {9 \times 52}{4} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {9 \times 13 \times 4} {4} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {9 \times 13 \times \cancel{4}} {\cancel{4}} \\\\
                                    &= 9 \times 13 \\\\
                                    &= 117 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$117 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

![papers/st-pauls-girls-school/2017/sample-paper-1/s02-q07-i00.png](/assets/papers/st-pauls-girls-school/2017/sample-paper-1/s02-q07-i00.png "papers/st-pauls-girls-school/2017/sample-paper-1/s02-q07-i00.png")

All the long edges of the shape above have the same length and each long edge is twice as long as each short edge. 
All angles are $90 \degree$ or $270 \degree$. If the area of the figure is $200 \ \text{cm}^2$, what is the perimeter?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%image%
<emptyline>
All the long edges of the shape above have the same length and each long edge is twice as long as each short edge. 
All angles are $90 \degree$ or $270 \degree$. If the area of the figure is $200 \ \text{cm}^2$, what is the perimeter?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

TODOIMAGE


*TODO:: Show the diagram and divide the rectangle into $4$ parts.*

*ABBR: TODO:: Add drawing ends.*


$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area}     &= \text{Area of 4 rectangles} \\\\
200             &= 4 \times (a \times 2a) \\\\
200             &= 4 \times 2a^2 \\\\
200             &= 8a^2 \\\\
8a^2            &= 200 \\\\
a^2             &= \dfrac {200} {8} \\\\
a^2             &= \dfrac {25 \times 8} {8} \\\\
a^2             &= \dfrac {25 \times \cancel 8} {\cancel 8} \\\\
a^2             &= 25 \\\\
a               &= \sqrt{25} \\\\
a               &= 5 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Perimeter}     &= \text{Length of 4 long sides} + \text{Length of 8 short sides}  \\\\
                     &= 4 \times a + 8 \times 2a \\\\
                     &= 4a + 16a \\\\
                     &= 20a \\\\
                     &= 20 \times 5 \\\\
                     &= 100 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$100 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

Work out the missing length.

![papers/st-pauls-girls-school/2017/sample-paper-1/s02-q08-i00.png](/assets/papers/st-pauls-girls-school/2017/sample-paper-1/s02-q08-i00.png "papers/st-pauls-girls-school/2017/sample-paper-1/s02-q08-i00.png")

<div class="workings">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

Let the length of rectangle A $= a$

Let the length of rectangle B $= b$

Let the missing length $= l$

Length of rectangle C $= a + b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times 4                                                                  &= 20 \\\\
4a                                                                          &= 20 \\\\
a                                                                           &= \dfrac {20} {4} \\\\
a                                                                           &= \dfrac {4 \times 5} {4} \\\\
a                                                                           &= \dfrac {\cancel {4} \times 5 } {\cancel {4}} \\\\
a                                                                           &= 5 \ \text{cm} \\\\
b \times 5                                                                  &= 14 \\\\
5b                                                                          &= 14 \\\\
b                                                                           &= \dfrac {14} {5} \\\\
l \times (a + b)                                                            &= 78 \\\\
l \times (5 + \dfrac {14} {5})                                              &= 78 \\\\
l \times (\dfrac {5 \times 5} {1 \times 5} + \dfrac {14} {5})               &= 78 \\\\
l \times (\dfrac {25} {5} + \dfrac {14} {5})                                &= 78 \\\\
l \times \dfrac {25 + 14} {5}                                               &= 78 \\\\
l \times \dfrac {39} {5}                                                    &= 78 \\\\
l                                                                           &= \dfrac {78 \times 5} {39} \\\\
l                                                                           &= \dfrac {39 \times 2 \times 5} {39} \\\\
l                                                                           &= \dfrac {\cancel {39} \times 2 \times 5} {\cancel {39}} \\\\
l                                                                           &= 2 \times 5 \\\\
l                                                                           &= 5 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Missing length $= 10 \ \text{cm}$. 
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$10 \ \text{cm}$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A rectangular room is twice as long as it is wide. The perimeter of the room is $36 \ \text{m}$. What is the length of the room?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A rectangular room is twice as long as it is wide. The perimeter of the room is $36 \ \text{m}$. What is the length of the room?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the width of room $= a$

Length of the room $= 2a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times (2a + a)                   &= 36 \\\\
2 \times 3a                         &= 36 \\\\
6a                                  &= 36 \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {36} {6} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {6 \times 6} {6} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {6} \times 6} {\cancel {6}} \\\\
a                                   &= 6 \ \text{m} \\\\
\text {Length of the rectangle}     &= 2a \\\\
                                    &= 2 \times 6 \\\\ 
                                    &= 12 \ \text{m}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$12 \ \text{m}$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A carpet measuring $4 \ \text{m}$ by $3 \ \text{m}$ covers $60\%$ of the floor area in a rectangular room.

What is the width of the room if the length is $5 \ \text{m}$?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A carpet measuring $4 \ \text{m}$ by $3 \ \text{m}$ covers $60\%$ of the floor area in a rectangular room.
<emptyline>
What is the width of the room if the length is $5 \ \text{m}$?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the width of the room $= w \ \text{m}$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of carpet}       &= 60\% \ \text{of Area of the room} \\\\
4 \times 3                  &= \dfrac {60} {100} \times (5 \times w) \\\\
12                          &= \dfrac {60 \times 5 \times w} {100} \\\\\
12                          &= \dfrac {20 \times 3 \times 5 \times w} {20 \times 5} \\\\\
12                          &= \dfrac {\cancel{20} \times 3 \times \cancel{5} \times w} {\cancel{20} \times \cancel{5}} \\\\\
12                          &= 3 \times w \\\\
12                          &= 3w \\\\
3w                          &= 12 \\\\
w                           &= \dfrac {12} {3} \\\\
w                           &= \dfrac {4 \times 3} {3} \\\\
w                           &= \dfrac {4 \times \cancel{3}} {\cancel{3}} \\\\
w                           &= 4 \ \text{m} \\\\
\text{Width of carpet}      &= 4 \ \text{m}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4 \ \text{m}$

</div>
</div>

- $49 \ \text{cm}$
- $98 \ \text{cm}$
- $28 \ \text{cm}$
- $20 \ \text{cm}$
- $14 \ \text{cm}$ 

</div>

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times a              &= 49 \\\\

a                       &= 7 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the perimeter of the square.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Perimeter}       &= 4 \times a \\\\
                        &= 4 \times 7 \\\\
                        &= 28 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A roll of wallpaper is $10 \ \text{m}$ long and $0.6 \ \text{m}$ wide. How many rolls of 
wallpaper are needed to cover a wall $3 \ \text{m}$ high and $8 \ \text{m}$ wide?

- $5$
- $4$
- $7$
- $10$
- $11$ 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A roll of wallpaper is $10 \ \text{m}$ long and $0.6 \ \text{m}$ wide. How many rolls of 
wallpaper are needed to cover a wall $3 \ \text{m}$ high and $8 \ \text{m}$ wide?
<emptyline>
- $5$
- $4$
- $7$
- $10$
- $11$ 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of rolls}  &= \dfrac {\text{Area of the Wall}} {\text{Area of a wallpaper roll}} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {8 \times 3} {10 \times 0.6} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {24} {6} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {6 \times 4} {6} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {\cancel {6} \times 4} {\cancel {6}} \\\\
                        &= 4
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="option" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Option**

<p>B</p>
</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="tipcodeblock_title">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A square piece of card has perimeter $28 \ \text{cm}$. 
Ann cuts the card into two rectangles. 
The perimeter of one of the rectangles is $16 \ \text{cm}$. 
What is the  perimeter of the other rectangle?

- $26$
- $16$
- $14$
- $24$
- $20$ 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A square piece of card has perimeter $28 \ \text{cm}$. 
Ann cuts the card into two rectangles. 
The perimeter of one of the rectangles is $16 \ \text{cm}$. 
What is the  perimeter of the other rectangle?
<emptyline>
- $26$
- $16$
- $14$
- $24$
- $20$ 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of the square $= a$

Let the width of the first rectangle $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
4 \times a              &= 28 \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {28} {4} \\\\ 
a                       &= \dfrac {4 \times 7} {4} \\\\ 
a                       &= \dfrac {\cancel 4 \times 7} {\cancel 4} \\\\
a                       &= 7  \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Perimeter of first rectangle} &= 16 \\\\
2 \times (7 + b)                    &= 16 \\\\
7 + b                               &= \dfrac {16} {2} \\\\ 
7 + b                               &= \dfrac {2 \times 8} {2} \\\\ 
7 + b                               &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 8} {\cancel 2} \\\\
7 + b                               &= 8 \\\\
b                                   &= 8 - 7 \\\\
b                                   &= 1 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Perimeter of second rectangle} &=  2 \times (7 + (7-1)) \\\\
                                     &=  2 \times (7 + 6) \\\\
                                     &=  2 \times 13 \\\\
                                     &=  26 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="option" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Option**

<p>A</p>
</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$26 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

The area of the parallelogram is $38 \ \text{cm}^2$. Find the length of its base.

![papers/streatham-and-clapham-high-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q13-i00.png](/assets/papers/streatham-and-clapham-high-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q13-i00.png "papers/streatham-and-clapham-high-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q13-i00.png")

- $9.5 \ \text{cm}$
- $8.5 \ \text{cm}$
- $7.5 \ \text{cm}$
- $7.25 \ \text{cm}$
- $9.25 \ \text{cm}$

</div>

$

b                             &= 9.5 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Length of the base of the parallelogram $= 9.5 \ \text{cm}$.

- $20 \ \text{cm}$
- $40 \ \text{cm}$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Here are three squares that overlap.

![papers/sydenham-high-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q16-i00.png](/assets/papers/sydenham-high-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q16-i00.png "papers/sydenham-high-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q16-i00.png")

The non-overlapping parts of the squares have a total area of $90 \ \text{cm}^{2}$.

The areas of overlapping parts are $2 \ \text{cm}^{2}$, 
$3 \ \text{cm}^{2}$ and $4 \ \text{cm}^{2}$.

Work out the area of one of the squares. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Here are three squares that overlap.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
The non-overlapping parts of the squares have a total area of $90 \ \text{cm}^{2}$.
<emptyline>
The areas of overlapping parts are $2 \ \text{cm}^{2}$, 
$3 \ \text{cm}^{2}$ and $4 \ \text{cm}^{2}$.
<emptyline>
Work out the area of one of the squares. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

area of non-overlapping squares $=90\ \text{cm}^{2}$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{area of non-overlapping of one squares} &= \dfrac{90}{3} \ \text{cm}^{2} \\\\ 
                                              &= \dfrac{90}{3} \\\\
                                              &= \dfrac{30 \times 3}{3} \\\\
                                              &= \dfrac{30 \times \cancel 3}{\cancel 3} \\\\
                                              &= 30\ \text{cm}^{2}
\end{aligned}
$

area of overlapping parts $=2\ \text{cm}^{2}, 3\ \text{cm}^{2}, 4\ \text{cm}^{2}$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{area of one square} &= \text{area of non-overlapping of one square} + \text{area of 2 overlapping parts} \\\\
                          &= 30 + 2 +3 \\\\
                          &= 35\ \text{cm}^{2}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$35\ \text{cm}^{2}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Four strips of paper are stuck on a table as shown. Each one is a rectangle that is $12 \ \text{cm}$ long and $2 \ \text{cm}$ wide.

![papers/sydenham-high-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q30-i00.png](/assets/papers/sydenham-high-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q30-i00.png "papers/sydenham-high-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q30-i00.png")

What area of the table is covered? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Four strips of paper are stuck on a table as shown. Each one is a rectangle that is $12 \ \text{cm}$ long and $2 \ \text{cm}$ wide.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
What area of the table is covered? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

Since the rectangles are overlapping at four places, we need to subtract those area from the total.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of the table covered} &= \text {Total area of rectangles} - \text {overlapping area} \\\\
                                  &= (12 \times 2 \times 4) - (2 \times 2 \times 4) \\\\
                                  &= 96 - 16 \\\\
                                  &= 80 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$80 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

A cuboid has faces with areas of $24 \ \text{cm}^{2}, 32 \ \text{cm}^{2}$ and $48 \ \text{cm}^{2}$.

What are the lengths of its edges? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A cuboid has faces with areas of $24 \ \text{cm}^{2}, 32 \ \text{cm}^{2}$ and $48 \ \text{cm}^{2}$.
<emptyline>
What are the lengths of its edges? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the length of first edge of cuboid $= l$

Let the length of second edge of cuboid $= w$

Let the length of third edge cuboid $= h$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
l \times w                                      &= 24 \\\\
w                                               &= \dfrac {24} {l} \\\\
w \times h                                      &= 32 \\\\
\dfrac {24} {l} \times h                        &= 32 \\\\
\dfrac {24h} {l}                                &= 32 \\\\
24h                                             &= 32 \times l \\\\
h                                               &= \dfrac {32 \times l} {24} \\\\
l \times h                                      &= 48 \\\\
l \times \dfrac{32 \times l} {24}               &= 48 \\\\
\dfrac{l \times 32 \times l} {24}               &= 48 \\\\
\dfrac{32 \times l^2} {24}                      &= 48 \\\\
32 \times l^2                                   &= 48 \times 24 \\\\
l^2                                             &= \dfrac {48 \times 24} {32} \\\\
l^2                                             &= \dfrac {16 \times 3 \times 2 \times 12} {16 \times 2} \\\\
l^2                                             &= \dfrac {\cancel {16} \times 3 \times \cancel {2} \times 12} {\cancel {16} \times \cancel {2}} \\\\
l^2                                             &= 3 \times 12 \\\\
l^2                                             &= 36 \\\\
l                                               &= \sqrt {36} \\\\
l                                               &= 6 \ \text{cm} \\\\
w                                               &= \dfrac {24} {6} \\\\
w                                               &= \dfrac {6 \times 4} {6} \\\\
w                                               &= \dfrac {\cancel {6} \times 4} {\cancel {6}} \\\\
w                                               &= 4 \ \text{cm} \\\\
l \times h                                      &= 48 \\\\
6 \times h                                      &= 48 \\\\
h                                               &= \dfrac {48} {6} \\\\
h                                               &= \dfrac {6 \times 8} {6} \\\\
h                                               &= \dfrac {\cancel {6} \times 8} {\cancel {6}} \\\\
h                                               &= 8 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Length of the edges of the cuboid are $6 \ \text{cm}, \ 4 \ \text{cm}, \ 8 \ \text{cm}$.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$6 \ \text{cm}, \ 4 \ \text{cm}, \ 8 \ \text{cm}$

</div>

**Question**

How many strips do I need in total?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many strips do I need in total?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
_no_dot
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The lawn measurement is given in $\text{metres}$ while the strip measurement is given in $\text{cm}$.

Let's convert the lawn measurements into $\text{cm}$.

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Total strips required}           &= \dfrac {\text {Width of lawn}} {\text {Width of strips}} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {20 \ \text {meters}} {50 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {20 \times 100 \ \text{cm}} {50 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {20 \times 100} {50} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {20 \times 50 \times 2} {50} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {20 \times \cancel {50} \times 2} {\cancel {50}} \\\\
                                        &= 20 \times 2 \\\\
                                        &= 40
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$40$

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I can push my lawnmower at a constant speed of $30 \ \text{metres per minute}$ and it takes me an extra $15 \ \text{seconds}$ 
to turn the mower round at the end of every strip. The mower itself takes $15 \ \text{seconds}$ 
to turn on. How long does it take me to mow my lawn?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I can push my lawnmower at a constant speed of $30 \ \text{metres per minute}$ and it takes me an extra $15 \ \text{seconds}$ 
to turn the mower round at the end of every strip. The mower itself takes $15 \ \text{seconds}$ 
to turn on. How long does it take me to mow my lawn?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
_no_dot
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The lawnmower speed is given in $\text{metres per minute}$ while the mower turn speed is given in $\text{seconds}$.

Let's convert the lawnmower speed into $\text{meters per seconds}$.

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Time taken to mow the lawn}          &= \text {(Number of strips)} \times 1 \ \text {min} + \text {(Number of strips - 1)} \times 15 \ \text {sec} + 15 \ \text {sec} \\\\
                                            &= 40 \times 1 \times 60 \ \text {sec} + 39 \times  15 \ \text {sec} + 15 \ \text {sec} \\\\
                                            &= 40 \times 1 \times 60  + 39 \times  15 + 15 \\\\
                                            &= 2400 + 585 + 15 \\\\
                                            &= 3000 \ \text {seconds} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {3000} {60} \ \text {minutes} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {60 \times 50} {60} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {\cancel {60} \times 50} {\cancel {60}} \\\\
                                            &= 50 \ \text {minutes}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$50 \ \text {minutes}$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

The area of land which consists of forest but no mountain is $32 \ \text{km}^2$ and the area which is both forest and 
mountain is $6 \ \text{km}^2$. The area of water is $67 \ \text{km}^2$. 

Work out the area of land which consists of mountain but no forest.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The area of land which consists of forest but no mountain is $32 \ \text{km}^2$ and the area which is both forest and 
mountain is $6 \ \text{km}^2$. The area of water is $67 \ \text{km}^2$. 
<emptyline>
Work out the area of land which consists of mountain but no forest.
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

\text {Area}                 &= \text {Land} - \text {Water} - \text {Forest} \\\\
                             &= 160 - 67 - (32 + 6) \\\\
                             &= 160 - 67 - 38 \\\\
                             &= 55 \ \text {km} ^ 2
\end{aligned}
$

Area of land which consists of mountain but no forest $= 55 \ \text {km}^2$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find the area of a square with a perimeter of $36 \ \text{cm}$.

Find the perimeter of a square with an area of $121 \ \text{cm}^2$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find the area of a square with a perimeter of $36 \ \text{cm}$.
<emptyline>
Find the perimeter of a square with an area of $121 \ \text{cm}^2$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of the square $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
4 \times a           &= 36\\\\
a                    &= \dfrac {36} {4} \\\\
a                    &= \dfrac {9 \times 4} {4} \\\\
a                    &= \dfrac {9 \times \cancel{4}} {\cancel{4}} \\\\
a                    &= 9 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's calculate the area of square.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area}    &= 9 \times 9 \\\\
                &= 81 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of the square $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times a             &= 121 \\\\
a^2                    &= 121 \\\\
a                      &= \sqrt {121} \\\\
a                      &= 11 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's calculate the perimeter of square.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Perimeter}      &= 4 \times 11 \\\\
                       &= 44 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$81 \ \text{cm}^2 $

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$44 \ \text{cm}$

</div>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the side of the square $= a$
<emptyline>
As per the question,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
a \times a             &= 121 \\\\
a^2                    &= 121 \\\\
a                      &= \sqrt {121} \\\\
a                      &= 11 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Let's calculate the perimeter of square.
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Perimeter}      &= 4 \times 11 \\\\
                       &= 44 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

**Question**

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of A}        &= 12 \times 4 \\\\
                        &= 48 \ \text {square unit} \\\\
\text{Perimeter of A}   &= 2 \times (12 + 4) \\\\
                        &= 2 \times 16 \\\\
                        &= 32 \ \text{unit} \\\\
\text{Area of B}        &= (8 \times 3) + (8 \times 3) \\\\
                        &= 24 + 24 \\\\
                        &= 48 \ \text {square unit} \\\\
\text{Perimeter of B}   &= 11 \times 2 + 8 \times 2 \\\\
                        &= 22 + 16 \\\\
                        &= 38 \ \text {unit} \\\\
\text{Area of C}        &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 4 \times 8 \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 2 \times 2 \times 8 \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {1} {\cancel 2} \times \cancel 2 \times 2 \times 8 \\\\
                        &= 8 \times 2 \\\\
                        &= 16 \ \text {square unit} \\\\
\text{Perimeter of C}   &= 4 + 8 + \sqrt{16+ 64}\\\\
                        &= 12 + \sqrt{80} \ \text {unit} \\\\
\text{Area of D}        &= (2 \times 6) + (2 \times 4) + (2 \times 6) \\\\
                        &= 12 + 8 + 12 \\\\
                        &= 32\ \text {square unit} \\\\
\text{Perimeter of B}   &= 10 \times 2 + 6 \times 2  \\\\
                        &= 20 + 12 \\\\
                        &= 32 \ \text {unit} \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$50 \ \text{centimetres}$ wide.

How many paving stones does Stuart need to buy?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">

_no_dot
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The patio measurement is given in $\text{meters}$ while the stone measurement is given in $\text{cm}$.

Let's convert the patio measurements into $\text{cm}$.

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of stones} &= \dfrac {\text{Area of the patio}} {\text{Area of a stone}} \\\\
                         &= \dfrac {5 \ \text{m} \times 5 \ \text{m}} {50 \ \text{cm} \times 50 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                         &= \dfrac {5 \times 100 \ \text{cm} \times 5 \times 100 \ \text{cm}} {50 \ \text{cm} \times 50 \ \text{cm}} \\\\
                         &= \dfrac {5 \times 100 \times 5 \times 100} {50  \times 50} \\\\
                         &= \dfrac {5 \times 10 \times 10 \times 5 \times 10 \times 10} {5 \times 10 \times 5 \times 10} \\\\
                         &= \dfrac {\cancel {5} \times \cancel {10} \times 10 \times \cancel {5} \times \cancel {10} \times 10} {\cancel {5} \times \cancel {10} \times \cancel {5} \times \cancel {10}} \\\\
                         &= 10 \times 10 \\\\
                         &= 100
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$100$

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Stuart has $\pounds 200$ left after buying the paving stones. Stuart wants to put a picket fence around **three sides** of his patio.

Each panel of picket fencing is $1 \ \text{metre}$ long and costs $\pounds 10.50$. 
Stuart will also have to pay a delivery charge of $\pounds 5$ regardless of the number of panels of picket fencing he purchases.

How much money does Stuart have left after buying the picket fencing?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Stuart has $\pounds 200$ left after buying the paving stones. Stuart wants to put a picket fence around **three sides** of his patio.
<emptyline>
Each panel of picket fencing is $1 \ \text{metre}$ long and costs $\pounds 10.50$. 
Stuart will also have to pay a delivery charge of $\pounds 5$ regardless of the number of panels of picket fencing he purchases.
<emptyline>
How much money does Stuart have left after buying the picket fencing?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of panels}            &= 3 \times \dfrac {\text {Length of a side}} {\text {Length of a panel}} \\\\
                                    &= 3 \times \dfrac {5} {1} \\\\
                                    &= 3 \times 5 \\\\
                                    &= 15 \\\\
\text {Cost of panels}              &= 10.50 \times 15 \\\\
                                    &= \pounds 157.5 \\\\
\text {Money left}                  &= \text {Total Money} - \text {Cost of panels} - \text {Delivery charge} \\\\
                                    &= 200 - 157.5 - 5 \\\\
                                    &= \pounds 37.5
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$\pounds 37.5$

**Question**

By thinking of two different ways to work out the area of the triangle, calculate the length of arrow.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">By thinking of two different ways to work out the area of the triangle, calculate the length of arrow.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the length of the arrow $= h$

As, per the diagram,

$
\beign{aligned}
\dfrac {1} {2} \times 10 \times h        &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 8 \times 6 \\\\
\dfrac {10 \times h} {2}                 &= \dfrac {8 \times 6} {2}  \\\\
h                                        &= \dfrac {8 \times 6 \times 2} {2 \times 10} \\\\
h                                        &= \dfrac {8 \times 3 \times 2 \times 2} {2 \times 10} \\\\
h                                        &= \dfrac {8 \times 3 \times 2 \times 2} {2 \times 2 \times 5} \\\\
h                                        &= \dfrac {8 \times 3 \times \cancel {2} \times \cancel {2}} {\cancel {2} \times \cancel {2} \times 5} \\\\
h                                        &= \dfrac {8 \times 3} {5} \\\\
h                                        &= \dfrac {24} {5} \\\\
h                                        &= 4.8 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Length of the arrow $= 4.8 \ \text{cm}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4.8 \ \text{cm}$

</div>

![papers/the-independent-schools-examinations-board/2008/sample-paper-1/s01-q13-s02-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-independent-schools-examinations-board/2008/sample-paper-1/s01-q13-s02-i00.png "papers/the-independent-schools-examinations-board/2008/sample-paper-1/s01-q13-s02-i00.png")

Find the length of his new pen.

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

**Question**

Farmer Fred decides that he would like to build a square pen with his $15 \ \text{metres}$ of fence as shown below:

![papers/the-independent-schools-examinations-board/2008/sample-paper-1/s01-q13-s03-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-independent-schools-examinations-board/2008/sample-paper-1/s01-q13-s03-i00.png "papers/the-independent-schools-examinations-board/2008/sample-paper-1/s01-q13-s03-i00.png")

How long should each side be?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Farmer Fred decides that he would like to build a square pen with his $15 \ \text{metres}$ of fence as shown below:
<emptyline>
%image%

How long should each side be?
</code></pre>

**Working**

Let the length of side $= a$

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + a + a               &= 15 \\\\
3a                      &= 15 \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {15} {3} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {3 \times 5} {3} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {\cancel {3} \times 5} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                       &= 5 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Each side should be $5 \ \text{cm}$ long.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$5 \ \text{cm}$

<div class="workingcodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the length of side $= a$
<emptyline>
As per the diagram,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
a + a + a               &= 15 \\\\
3a                      &= 15 \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {15} {3} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {3 \times 5} {3} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {\cancel {3} \times 5} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                       &= 5 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Each side should be $5 \ \text{cm}$ long.
</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

\end{aligned}

Height $= 1 \ \text{m}$

Width $= 24 \ \text{m}$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A farmer wants to put a fence along one edge of his field,  
which is $480 \ \text{m}$ long. Every $4 \ \text{m}$, a post is needed to hold the rails up. 

![papers/the-kings-school-chester/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q22-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-kings-school-chester/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q22-i00.png "papers/the-kings-school-chester/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q22-i00.png")

How many posts does he need?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A farmer wants to put a fence along one edge of his field,  
which is $480 \ \text{m}$ long. Every $4 \ \text{m}$, a post is needed to hold the rails up. 
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
How many posts does he need?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Total posts}         &= \dfrac {\text {Length of fence}} {\text {Length for a post}} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {480} {4} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {4 \times 120} {4} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {\cancel {4} \times 120} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
                            &= 120
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$120$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The area of this rectangle is $24 \ \text{cm}^2$. What is its perimeter in cm?

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2008/group-1/s01-q29-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2008/group-1/s01-q29-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2008/group-1/s01-q29-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The area of this rectangle is $24 \ \text{cm}^2$. What is its perimeter in cm?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the length of the rectangle $= l$

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
l \times 4          &= 24 \\\\
4l                  &= 24 \\\\
l                   &= \dfrac {24} {4} \\\\
l                   &= \dfrac {4 \times 6} {4} \\\\
l                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {4} \times 6} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
l                   &= 6 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the perimeter of the rectangle.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Perimeter}       &= 2 \times (6 + 4) \\\\
                        &= 2 \times 10 \\\\
                        &= 20 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$20 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

4l                  &= 24 \\\\
l                   &= \dfrac {24} {4} \\\\
l                   &= \dfrac {4 \times 6} {4} \\\\
l                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {4} \times 6} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
l                   &= 6 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Let's find the perimeter of the rectangle.
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Perimeter}       &= 2 \times (6 + 4) \\\\
                        &= 2 \times 10 \\\\
                        &= 20 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

**Question**

What is the area of this shape?

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2009/group-1/s01-q20-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2009/group-1/s01-q20-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2009/group-1/s01-q20-i00.png")

</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>

<emptyline>

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

*ABBR: TODO:: Add drawing ends.*


As per the diagram, the shape can be divided into a triangle and a rectangle.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area}     &= \text{Area of the triangle} + \text{Area of the rectangle} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 4 \times 4 + 2 \times 4 \\\\
                &= \dfrac {4 \times 4} {2} + 8 \\\\
                &= \dfrac {2 \times 2 \times 4} {2} + 8 \\\\
                &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 2 \times 4} {\cancel {2}} + 8 \\\\
                &= 2 \times 4 + 8 \\\\
                &= 8 + 8 \\\\
                &= 16 \ \text{units}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$16 \ \text{units}^2$

</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What are the values of $\text{x}$ and $\text{y}?$
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
4 + x + 2           &= 8 \\\\
x + 6               &= 8 \\\\
x                   &= 8 - 6 \\\\
x                   &= 2 \ \text{cm} \\\\
y + (6 - 2 - 2) + y &= 14 \\\\
2y + 2              &= 14 \\\\
2y                  &= 14 - 2 \\\\
2y                  &= 12 \\\\
y                   &= \dfrac {12} {2} \\\\
y                   &= \dfrac {2 \times 6} {2} \\\\
y                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 6} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
y                   &= 6 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$x = 2 \ \text{cm} \ , y = 6 \ \text{cm}$

</div>

**Working**

Let the length of the side $= a$

Number of sides included in the shape $= 16$

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
16 \times a             &= 160 \\\\
16a                     &= 160 \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {160} {16} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {16 \times 10} {16} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {\cancel {16} \times 10} {\cancel {16}} \\\\
a                       &= 10 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Length of the side of each small square $= 10 \ \text{cm}$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A rectangle has an area of $60 \ \text{cm}^2$. Its length is $11\ \text{cm}$ more than its width.

What is the perimeter of the rectangle?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A rectangle has an area of $60 \ \text{cm}^2$. Its length is $11\ \text{cm}$ more than its width.
<emptyline>
What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: 

*Note*: The two equations form a quadratic equation.

*Note*: This is a quadratic equation.

Solving quadratic equations is beyond the scope and any such equations can be easily inferred by trial and error method.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the width of rectangle $= w$

Length $=11 + w$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(11 + w) \times w                  &= 60
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

Putting  $w = 4$,

$
\begin{aligned}
(11 + 4) \times 4                   &= 60 \\\\
15 \times 4                         &= 60 \\\\
60                                  &= 60 \\\\
\text {Width}                       &= 4 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Length}                      &= 11 + 4 \\\\
                                    &= 15 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Perimeter}                   &= 2 \times (15 + 4) \\\\
                                    &= 2 \times 19 \\\\
                                    &= 38 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$38 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>
