![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2009/group-2/s01-q28-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2009/group-2/s01-q28-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2009/group-2/s01-q28-i00.png")

Twelve rectangles, all the same size, are arranged to make a square, as shown in the diagram above.

Calculate the area of one of the rectangles.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%image%
<emptyline>
Twelve rectangles, all the same size, are arranged to make a square, as shown in the diagram above.
<emptyline>
Calculate the area of one of the rectangles.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of one rectangle}           &= \dfrac {\text {Area of larger square} - \text {Area of smaller square}} {\text {Number of rectangles}} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {50 \times 50 - 40 \times 40} {12} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {2500 - 1600} {12} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {900} {12} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {12 \times 75} {12} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {\cancel {12} \times 75} {\cancel {12}} \\\\
                                        &= 75 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$75 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A sweet is in the shape of a cube. It is made up of three layers of equal thickness, as shown in the diagram.
What fraction of the outside is black?

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2009/group-2/s01-q39-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2009/group-2/s01-q39-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2009/group-2/s01-q39-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A sweet is in the shape of a cube. It is made up of three layers of equal thickness, as shown in the diagram.
What fraction of the outside is black?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the length of edge of cube $= a$

As the cube has six faces,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of all faces} \ &= \text{Area of each face} \ \times 6 \\\\
&= a^2 \ \times 6 \\\\
&= 6a^2
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of black region} \ &= 4 \times (\dfrac{a}{3} \times a) \\\\
&= \dfrac{4a^2}{3}
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Fraction of black region} &= \dfrac{\text{Area of black region}\ }{\text{Area of all faces}\ } \\\\
&= \dfrac{\dfrac{4a^2}{3}}{6a^2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{4a^2}{3 \times 6a^2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{4 \cancel{a^2}}{18 \cancel{a^2}} \\\\
&= \dfrac{2}{9}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\dfrac{2}{9}$

</div>
</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the area of one of the triangles?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%

</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the height of the triangle $= h$

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
2h                              &= 4 \\\\
h                               &= \dfrac {4} {2} \\\\
h                               &= \dfrac {2 \times 2} {2} \\\\
h                               &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 2} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
h                               &= 2 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Area of one triangle}    &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 4 \times 2 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {4 \times 2} {2} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {4 \times \cancel {2}} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
                                &= 4 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is the length of one of its sides?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the length of one of its sides?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of the square (in $\text{cm}$) $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
4 \times a                      &= 36 \\\\
4a                              &= 36 \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {36} {4} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {4 \times 9} {4} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {\cancel {4} \times 9} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
a                               &= 9 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Length of the side of square $= 9 \ \text{cm}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$6 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many rectangles with a length of $3 \ \text{cm}$ and width 
of $1 \ \text{cm}$ would it take to fill the shape below with no overlapping?

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2011/group-1/s01-q31-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2011/group-1/s01-q31-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2011/group-1/s01-q31-i00.png")

</div>

of $1 \ \text{cm}$ would it take to fill the shape below with no overlapping?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">

As per the diagram, the shape can be divided into two rectangles.

$
\begin{aligned}

                                &= \dfrac {\text {Rectangle 1} + \text {Rectangle 2}} {\text {Area of a rectangle}} \\\\

                                &= 6
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Two identical square holes are cut from a rectangular sheet leaving an 
area of $58 \ \text{square centimetres}$. How long are the sides of the square?

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2011/group-2/s01-q29-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2011/group-2/s01-q29-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2011/group-2/s01-q29-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Two identical square holes are cut from a rectangular sheet leaving an 
area of $58 \ \text{square centimetres}$. How long are the sides of the square?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of the square hole $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of two square holes} &= \text{Area of the rectangular sheet} - \text{Left area} \\\\
2 \times a ^ 2                  &= 10 \times 9 - 58 \\\\
2 \times a ^ 2                  &= 90 - 58 \\\\
2 \times a ^ 2                  &= 32 \\\\
a ^ 2                           &= \dfrac {32} {2} \\\\
a ^ 2                           &= \dfrac {16 \times 2} {2} \\\\
a ^ 2                           &= \dfrac {16 \times \cancel {2}} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
a                               &= \sqrt 16 \\\\
a                               &= 4 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

The total area of his shape is $120 \ \text{cm}^2$.

What is the area of one triangle?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The total area of his shape is $120 \ \text{cm}^2$.
<emptyline>
What is the area of one triangle?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of one triangle}            &= \dfrac {\text {Total Area}} {\text {Number of triangles}} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {120} {4} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {4 \times 30} {4} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {\cancel {4} \times 30} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
                                        &= 30 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$30 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q24-s01-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q24-s01-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q24-s01-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Work out the area of the shape below, drawn on centimetre-squared paper.

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area} &= \text{Area of two triangles} + \text{Area of rectangle} \\\\
            &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 4 \times 1 + \dfrac {1} {2} \times 2 \times 1 + 1 \times 4 \\\\
            &= \dfrac {4} {2} + \dfrac {2} {2} +  4 \\\\
            &= \dfrac {2 \times 2} {2} + \dfrac {2} {2} +  4 \\\\
            &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 2} {\cancel 2} + \dfrac {\cancel 2} {\cancel 2} +  4 \\\\
            &= 2 + 1 + 4 \\\\
            &= 7 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$6$ cubes have been joined together to make the shape below.

The area of each face of the cubes is $1 \ \text{cm}^2$.

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q35-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q35-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q35-i00.png")

If the shape is dipped into a large pot of paint, what is the total 
area which will be covered in paint?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>

<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>

area which will be covered in paint?
</code></pre>

                          &= 26 \\\\
\text{Total area painted} &= 26 \times 1 \ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
                          &= 26 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

In the diagrams below, the square and rectangle have the same perimeter. 

The square has an area of $64 \ \text{cm}^2$.

The length of the rectangle is three times the width of the rectangle.

Work out the length of the rectangle.

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-2/s01-q35-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-2/s01-q35-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-2/s01-q35-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In the diagrams below, the square and rectangle have the same perimeter. 
<emptyline>
The square has an area of $64 \ \text{cm}^2$.
<emptyline>
The length of the rectangle is three times the width of the rectangle.
<emptyline>
Work out the length of the rectangle.
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of the square $= s$

Let the width of the rectangle $= w$

Length of the rectangle $= 3w$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
s \times s              &= 64 \\\\
s^2                     &= 64 \\\\
s                       &= \sqrt {64} \\\\
s                       &= 8 \ \text{cm} \\\\
2 \times (3w + w)       &= 4 \times s \\\\
2 \times 4w             &= 4 \times 8 \\\\
8w                      &= 4 \times 8 \\\\
w                       &= \dfrac {4 \times 8} {8} \\\\
w                       &= \dfrac {4 \times \cancel {8}} {\cancel {8}} \\\\
w                       &= 4 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Length}          &= 3 \times w \\\\
                        &= 3 \times 4 \\\\
                        &= 12 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$12 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="workings">

**Working**

The track measurement is given in $\text{meters}$ while the distance is given in $\text{kilometers}$.

Let's convert the distance into $\text{meters}$.

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Total rounds}  &= \dfrac {\text {Distance}} {\text {Perimeter}} \\\\
                      &= \dfrac {6 \ \text {kilometres}} {400 \ \text {metres}} \\\\
                      &= \dfrac {6 \times 1000 \ \text {metres}} {400 \ \text {metres}} \\\\
                      &= \dfrac {6 \times 1000} {400} \\\\
                      &= \dfrac {6000} {400} \\\\
                      &= \dfrac {400 \times 15} {400} \\\\
                      &= \dfrac {\cancel {400} \times 15} {\cancel {400}} \\\\
                      &= 15
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$15$

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A marathon course is $42.2 \ \text{km}$ long.

One marathon begins with $13.4 \ \text{km}$ running along country roads.

The runners then complete $2$ laps of equal length through a town.

To complete the race, the runners run around the running track $3$ times.

Work out the length of a lap through the town.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A marathon course is $42.2 \ \text{km}$ long.
<emptyline>
One marathon begins with $13.4 \ \text{km}$ running along country roads.
<emptyline>
The runners then complete $2$ laps of equal length through a town.
<emptyline>
To complete the race, the runners run around the running track $3$ times.
<emptyline>
Work out the length of a lap through the town.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
_no_dot
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The track length is given in $\text{meters}$ while the marathon length is given in $\text{kilometers}$.

Let's convert the track length into $\text{kilometers}$.

Let the length of a lap through town $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times \text {Length of a lap through town}  &= \text {Total length for the marathon} - (\text {Length of the the country roads} + 3 \times \text {Length of the running track}) \\\\
2a                                            &= 42.2 \ \text {kilometres} - (13.4 \ \text {kilometres} + 3 \times 400 \ \text {metres}) \\\\
2a                                            &= 42.2 \ \text {kilometres} - (13.4 \ \text {kilometres} + 3 \times \dfrac {400} {1000} \ \text {kilometres}) \\\\
2a                                            &= 42.2 - (13.4 + 3 \times 0.4) \\\\
2a                                            &= 42.2 - (13.4 + 1.2) \\\\
2a                                            &= 42.2 - 14.6 \\\\
2a                                            &= 56.8 \\\\
a                                             &= \dfrac {56.8} {2} \\\\
a                                             &= 28.4 \ \text {kilometres}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$28.4 \ \text {kilometres}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The shape below is made from squares.

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2014/group-2/s01-q36-s01-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2014/group-2/s01-q36-s01-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2014/group-2/s01-q36-s01-i00.png")

The perimeter of the shape is $100 \ \text{centimetres}$.

Work out the area of the shape.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The shape below is made from squares.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
The perimeter of the shape is $100 \ \text{centimetres}$.
<emptyline>
Work out the area of the shape.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of polygon} = \text{Sum of all sides}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of the square $= s$

Number of sides in the shape $= 20$

Number of squares $= 10$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
20 \times s         &= 100 \\\\
20s                 &= 100 \\\\
s                   &= \dfrac {100} {20} \\\\
s                   &= \dfrac {20 \times 5} {20} \\\\
s                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {20} \times 5} {\cancel {20}} \\\\
s                   &= 5 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Total Area}  &= 10 \times \text {Area of a square} \\\\
                    &= 10 \times 5 \times 5 \\\\
                    &= 250 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$250 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A square and equilateral triangle have the same perimeter.

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2015/group-1/s01-q30-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2015/group-1/s01-q30-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2015/group-1/s01-q30-i00.png")

Given that the area of the square is $36 \ \text{cm}^2$, work out the length of one side of the equilateral triangle.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A square and equilateral triangle have the same perimeter.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
Given that the area of the square is $36 \ \text{cm}^2$, work out the length of one side of the equilateral triangle.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of triangle} = \text{Sum of all sides}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the length of a side of a square $= a$

Let the length of a side of the equilateral triangle $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times a                                   &= 36 \\\\
a ^ 2                                        &= 36 \\\\
a                                            &= \sqrt {36} \\\\
a                                            &= 6 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Perimeter of the square}              &= 4 \times a \\\\
                                             &= 4 \times 6 \\\\
                                             &= 24 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Perimeter of equilateral triangle}    &= \text {Perimeter of square} \\\\
b + b + b                                    &= 24 \\\\
3b                                           &= 24 \\\\
b                                            &= \dfrac {24} {3} \\\\
b                                            &= \dfrac {8 \times 3} {3} \\\\
b                                            &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel 3} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
b                                            &= 8 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Length of one side of the equilateral triangle $= 8 \ \text{cm}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$8 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="tipcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Tips Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%empty%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="formulacodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="formulacodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Formulas Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">- rtq_abbr_formula_katex_area_square_expanded
- rtq_abbr_formula_katex_expanded_perimeter_square
- rtq_abbr_formula_katex_expanded_perimeter_triangle
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="workingcodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the length of a side of a square $= a$
<emptyline>
Let the length of a side of the equilateral triangle $= b$
<emptyline>
As per the question,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
a \times a                                   &= 36 \\\\
a ^ 2                                        &= 36 \\\\
a                                            &= \sqrt {36} \\\\
a                                            &= 6 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Perimeter of the square}              &= 4 \times a \\\\
                                             &= 4 \times 6 \\\\
                                             &= 24 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Perimeter of equilateral triangle}    &= \text {Perimeter of square} \\\\
b + b + b                                    &= 24 \\\\
3b                                           &= 24 \\\\
b                                            &= \dfrac {24} {3} \\\\
b                                            &= \dfrac {8 \times 3} {3} \\\\
b                                            &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel 3} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
b                                            &= 8 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Length of one side of the equilateral triangle $= 8 \ \text{cm}$
</code></pre>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The shape below is made from two overlapping rectangles.

One rectangle measures $5 \ \text{cm}$ by $4 \ \text{cm}$.

The other measures $8 \ \text{cm}$ by $6 \ \text{cm}$.

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2015/group-2/s01-q35-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2015/group-2/s01-q35-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2015/group-2/s01-q35-i00.png")

Given that the area of the section shaded black is $15 \ \text{cm}^2$, work out the area of the section shaded grey.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The shape below is made from two overlapping rectangles.
<emptyline>
One rectangle measures $5 \ \text{cm}$ by $4 \ \text{cm}$.
<emptyline>
The other measures $8 \ \text{cm}$ by $6 \ \text{cm}$.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
Given that the area of the section shaded black is $15 \ \text{cm}^2$, work out the area of the section shaded grey.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of grey section}            &= \text {Area of larger rectangle} - (\text {Area of smaller rectangle} - \text {Area of black section}) \\\\
                                        &= 6 \times 8 - (4 \times 5 - 15) \\\\
                                        &= 48 - (20 - 15) \\\\
                                        &= 48 - 5 \\\\
                                        &= 43 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$43 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A square has perimeter $20 \ \text{cm}$.

Work out the area of the square.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A square has perimeter $20 \ \text{cm}$.
<emptyline>
Work out the area of the square.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the length of a side of square $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
4 \times a                  &= 20 \\\\
a                           &= \dfrac {20} {4} \\\\
a                           &= \dfrac {5 \times 4} {4} \\\\
a                           &= \dfrac {5 \times \cancel {4}} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
a                           &= 5 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Area the square}     &= a \times a \\\\
                            &= 5 \times 5 \\\\
                            &= 25 \ \text{cm} ^ 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$25 \ \text{cm} ^ 2$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

Rectangular stickers measure $3 \ \text{cm}$ by $2 \ \text{cm}$.

Susan wants to cover the front of the card with stickers, without any overlapping.

What is the maximum number of stickers she can fit on the front of the card?

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The diagram shows two squares. The larger square has perimeter $16 \ \text{cm}$.

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2016/group-2/s01-q35-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2016/group-2/s01-q35-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2016/group-2/s01-q35-i00.png")


What is the **area** of the smaller, white square?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The diagram shows two squares. The larger square has perimeter $16 \ \text{cm}$.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>

What is the **area** of the smaller, white square?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times \text{side}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
4 \times a &= 16 \ \text{cm} \\\\
a          &= \dfrac {16} {4} \\\\
a          &= \dfrac {4 \times 4} {4} \\\\
a          &= \dfrac {\cancel 4 \times 4} {\cancel 4} \\\\
a          &= 4 \ \text{cm} 
\end{aligned}          
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of bigger square}  &= 4 \times 4 \\\\
                              &= 16 \ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
\text{Area of smaller square} &= \dfrac{\text{Area of bigger square}}{2} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac{16} {2} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {8 \times 2} {2} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                              &= 8 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}          
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$8 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$
\begin{aligned}
4 \times a &= 16 \ \text{cm} \\\\
a          &= \dfrac {16} {4} \\\\
a          &= \dfrac {4 \times 4} {4} \\\\
a          &= \dfrac {\cancel 4 \times 4} {\cancel 4} \\\\
a          &= 4 \ \text{cm} 
\end{aligned}          
$
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of bigger square}  &= 4 \times 4 \\\\
                              &= 16 \ \text{cm}^2 \\\\
\text{Area of smaller square} &= \dfrac{\text{Area of bigger square}}{2} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac{16} {2} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {8 \times 2} {2} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                              &= 8 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}          
$
</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is the **maximum** number of matchboxes that could fit, in one layer, onto a tray that is 
$20 \ \text{cm}$ long and $15 \ \text{cm}$ wide?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the **maximum** number of matchboxes that could fit, in one layer, onto a tray that is 
$20 \ \text{cm}$ long and $15 \ \text{cm}$ wide?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of Matchboxes}    &= \dfrac {\text {Area of tray}} {\text {Area of the base of matchbox}} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {20 \times 15} {3 \times 5} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {20 \times 3 \times 5} {3 \times 5} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {20 \times \cancel {3} \times \cancel {5}} {\cancel {3} \times \cancel {5}} \\\\
                                &= 20
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$20$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is the maximum number of matchboxes that could be fitted into a box measuring $18 \ \text{cm}$ by $25 \ \text{cm}$ by $10 \ \text{cm}$?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the maximum number of matchboxes that could be fitted into a box measuring $18 \ \text{cm}$ by $25 \ \text{cm}$ by $10 \ \text{cm}$?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%

</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Volume of a cuboid} = \text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{height}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of matchboxes}            &= \dfrac {\text {Volume of box}} {\text {Volume of a matchbox}} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {18 \times 25 \times 10} {1 \times 3 \times 5} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {3 \times 6 \times 5 \times 5 \times 10} {3 \times 5} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {\cancel {3} \times 6 \times \cancel {5} \times 5 \times 10} {\cancel {3} \times \cancel {5}} \\\\
                                        &= 6 \times 5 \times 10 \\\\
                                        &= 300
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$300$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Rodger has seven cubes, each one with edges $1 \ \text{cm}$ 
long. He glues one face of each of six of the cubes, and 
sticks them, one to each face of the seventh. 

He then paints the shape he has made. What area is painted?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Rodger has seven cubes, each one with edges $1 \ \text{cm}$ 
long. He glues one face of each of six of the cubes, and 
sticks them, one to each face of the seventh. 
<emptyline>
He then paints the shape he has made. What area is painted?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question, 

The seventh cube (the cube in the centre) has all of its faces covered.

For the rest of $6$ cubes, one of their face is glued to the seventh cube. So that leaves $5$ faces per cube for painting.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Total faces}      &= 6 \times 5 \\\\
                        &= 30
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
1 \ \text{Face area}        &= 1 \times 1 \ \text{cm}^2\\\\
30 \ \text{Faces area}    &= 30 \times 1  \ \text{cm}^2\\\\
                        &= 30  \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$

Painted area $= 30 \ \text{cm}^2$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$30 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The distance all the way round the outside of my bicycle wheel is known as the circumference. It is about three times the distance across the middle of the wheel, known as the diameter.

![papers/the-manchester-grammar-school/2012/arithmetic-2/s01-q10-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-manchester-grammar-school/2012/arithmetic-2/s01-q10-i00.png "papers/the-manchester-grammar-school/2012/arithmetic-2/s01-q10-i00.png")

So if Andrew has a wheel with diameter $50 \ \text{centimetres}$, its circumference would be about $150 \ \text{cm}$ or $1.5 \ \text{metres}$ and it would take $100$ turns of the wheel to travel a distance of $150 \ \text{m}$ and $1000$ turns to travel $1.5 \ \text{kilometres}$.

Using this approximation that $\bold { \textbf{Circumference} = 3 \times \textbf{diameter} }$

</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many metres would Andrew travel in $60$ turns of the wheel?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many metres would Andrew travel in $60$ turns of the wheel?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
100 \ \text {Turns}             &= 150 \ \text{m} \\\\
1 \ \text {Turn}                &= \dfrac {150} {100} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {50 \times 3} {50 \times 2} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {\cancel {50} \times 3} {\cancel {50} \times 2} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {3} {2} \\\\
                                &= 1.5 \ \text{m} \\\\
60 \ \text {Turns}              &= 60 \times 1.5 \\\\
                                &= 6 \times 15 \\\\
                                &= 90  \ \text{m}
\end{aligned}
$

Andrew travels $90  \ \text{m}$ in $60$ turns of the wheel.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$90  \ \text{m}$

**Question**

Andrew's great-great-grandfather took part in the same race over a hundred years ago, but the large wheel on his penny-farthing bicycle was $2 \ \text{metres}$ across.

How many turns of this large wheel were required to complete the race?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

**Working**

Diameter of wheel $d = 2 \ \text{metres}$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Circumference} &= 3 \times d \\\\
                     &= 3 \times 2 \\\\
                     &= 6 \ \text{m}
\end{aligned}
$

Distance travelled $= 75 \ \text{km}$ 

Distance travelled = No. of turns $\times$ circumference

Let the the Number of turns $= x$

$
\begin{aligned}
x  &= \dfrac {75 \ \text{km}}{6 \ \text{m}} \\\\
x  &= \dfrac {75 \times 1000}{6} \\\\
x  &= \dfrac {75000}{6} \\\\
x  &= \dfrac {12500 \times 6}{6} \\\\
x  &= \dfrac {12500 \times \cancel 6}{\cancel 6} \\\\
x  &= 12500 \ \text {Turns}
\end{aligned}
$

It would take him $12500$ Turns to cover $75 \ \text{km}$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Nigel folds a **__square__** piece of paper in half to give a rectangle which has a perimeter of $36 \ \text{cm}$. What is the area of the original square?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Nigel folds a **__square__** piece of paper in half to give a rectangle which has a perimeter of $36 \ \text{cm}$. What is the area of the original square?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of the square (in $\text{cm}$) $= a$ 

Length of the rectangle $= a$

Width of the rectangle $= \dfrac {a} { 2 }$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times ( a + \dfrac {a} {2})                       &= 36 \\\\
2 \times (\dfrac {2a + a} {2})                       &= 36 \\\\
\cancel{2} \times \dfrac {2a + a} {\cancel {2}}      &= 36 \\\\
2a + a                                               &= 36 \\\\
3a                                                   &= 36 \\\\
a                                                    &= \dfrac {36} { 3 } \\\\
a                                                    &= \dfrac {12 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a                                                    &= \dfrac {12 \times \cancel {3}} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                                                    &= 12 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the area of the square.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area}     &= 12 \times 12 \\\\
                &= 144 \ \text{cm}^{2}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$144 \ \text{cm}^{2}$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

Ahmed's sheet of paper is $8 \ \text{cm}$ by $7 \ \text{cm}$. He cuts out a square with sides of length $5 \ \text{cm}$. 
What area of paper is remaining when he has cut out his square?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Ahmed's sheet of paper is $8 \ \text{cm}$ by $7 \ \text{cm}$. He cuts out a square with sides of length $5 \ \text{cm}$. 
What area of paper is remaining when he has cut out his square?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$

                            &= 31 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Bella's sheet of paper is $11 \ \text{cm}$ by $12 \ \text{cm}$. After her square is cut out, the area of paper she is left with is $68 \ \text{cm}^2$.  What is the length of each side of the square she cuts out?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Bella's sheet of paper is $11 \ \text{cm}$ by $12 \ \text{cm}$. After her square is cut out, the area of paper she is left with is $68 \ \text{cm}^2$.  What is the length of each side of the square she cuts out?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the side of the square $= s$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Remaining Area}      &= \text {Area of sheet} - \text {Area of square} \\\\
68                          &= 11 \times 12 - s \times s \\\\
68                          &= 132 - s^2 \\\\
s^2                         &= 132 - 68 \\\\
s^2                         &= 64 \\\\
s                           &= \sqrt {64} \\\\
s                           &= 8 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Length of the side of square that Bella cuts out $= 8 \ \text{cm}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$8 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Chris has an area of $23 \ \text{cm}^2$ of paper left when he cuts a square with sides of $7 \ \text{cm}$ from his sheet of paper.
If his rectangular sheet of paper is $8 \ \text{cm}$ wide, how long is it?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Chris has an area of $23 \ \text{cm}^2$ of paper left when he cuts a square with sides of $7 \ \text{cm}$ from his sheet of paper.
If his rectangular sheet of paper is $8 \ \text{cm}$ wide, how long is it?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the length of the sheet $= l$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Area of sheet} - \text {Area of square}    &= \text {Remaining Area} \\\\
l \times 8 - 7 \times 7                           &= 23 \\\\
8l - 49                                           &= 23 \\\\
8l                                                &= 23 + 49 \\\\
8l                                                &= 72 \\\\
l                                                 &= \dfrac {72} {8} \\\\
l                                                 &= \dfrac {8 \times 9} {8} \\\\
l                                                 &= \dfrac {\cancel {8} \times 9} {\cancel {8}} \\\\
l                                                 &= 9 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Length of the side of sheet $= 9 \ \text{cm}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$9 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

because $4 \ \text{cm} \times 2.5 = 10 \ \text{cm}$

**Question**

Find the length of a third block if the **__perimeter__** of one of its faces measured using its length and width is $42 \ \text{cm}$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find the length of a third block if the **__perimeter__** of one of its faces measured using its length and width is $42 \ \text{cm}$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the width $=$ w

length $= 2.5$ l

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times (w + 2.5w) &= 42 \\\\
2 \times 3.5w       &= 42 \\\\
3.5w                &= \dfrac {42}{2} \\\\
w                   &= \dfrac {42}{2 \times 3.5} \\\\
w                   &= \dfrac {42 \times 10}{2 \times 3.5 \times 10} \\\\
w                   &= \dfrac {42 \times 10}{2 \times 35} \\\\
w                   &= \dfrac {7 \times 6 \times 2 \times 5}{2 \times 7 \times 5} \\\\
w                   &= \dfrac {\cancel 7 \times 6 \times \cancel 2 \times \cancel 5}{\cancel 2 \times \cancel 7 \times \cancel 5} \\\\
w                   &= 6 \ \text{cm} 
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Length}  &= 2.5 \times w \\\\
                &= 2.5 \times 6 \\\\
                &= 15 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Length is $=15 \ \text{cm}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$15 \ \text{cm}$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A rectangle has an area of $70 \ \text{cm}^2$ and a perimeter of $38 \ \text{cm}$. What is the length of the **shortest** side of the rectangle?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A rectangle has an area of $70 \ \text{cm}^2$ and a perimeter of $38 \ \text{cm}$. What is the length of the **shortest** side of the rectangle?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$

- ABBR: $\text{Perimeter of rectangle} = 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the width of the rectangle (in $\text{cm}$) $= w$

Let the length of the rectangle (in $\text{cm}$) $= l$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
l \times w          &= 70 \\\\
2 \times (l + w)    &= 38 \\\\
l + w               &= \dfrac {38}{2} \\\\
l + w               &= 19
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

- Both the numbers should be smaller than $19$
- The product of the $2$ numbers is $70$ 
- The sum of the $2$ numbers is $19$.

Factors of $70 = 1, 2, 5, 7, 10, 14, 35, 70$

| Factors   |  Sum  | Numbers $< 19$    |
|:-------:  |:----: |:---------------:  |
| $2, 35$   | $37$  |        No         |
| $5, 14$   | $19$  |       Yes         |

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Two rectangles ABCD and PQRS are shown below:

![papers/the-perse-school/sample/specimen-paper-1/s01-q20-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-perse-school/sample/specimen-paper-1/s01-q20-i00.png "papers/the-perse-school/sample/specimen-paper-1/s01-q20-i00.png")

$AD = 3 \ \text{cm}$ 

$AB = 5 \ \text{cm}$

$PQ = 2 \ \text{cm}$

$PS = 2 \ \text{cm}$

$BR = 1 \ \text{cm}$

Calculate the shaded area.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Two rectangles ABCD and PQRS are shown below:
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
$AD = 3 \ \text{cm}$ 
<emptyline>
$AB = 5 \ \text{cm}$
<emptyline>
$PQ = 2 \ \text{cm}$
<emptyline>
$PS = 2 \ \text{cm}$
<emptyline>
$BR = 1 \ \text{cm}$
<emptyline>
Calculate the shaded area.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of rectangle} = \text{length} \times \text{width}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the diagram,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of shaded region}        &= \text{Area of ABCD} - \text{Area of rectangle inside ABCD} \\\\
                                    &= AB \times AD - QB \times QP \\\\
                                    &= AB \times AD - ((PS - BR) \times QP) \\\\
                                    &= 5 \times 3 - (2 - 1) \times 2 \\\\
                                    &= 5 \times 3 - 1 \times 2 \\\\
                                    &= 15 - 2 \\\\
                                    &= 13 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$13 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area}      &= \dfrac{1} {2} \times 8 \times 12 \\\\
                 &= \dfrac{8 \times 12} {2}\\\\
                 &= \dfrac{2 \times 4 \times 12} {2}\\\\
                 &= \dfrac{\cancel 2 \times 4 \times 12} {\cancel 2}\\\\
                 &= 12 \times 4 \\\\
                 &= 48 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

![papers/the-perse-school/sample/specimen-paper-3/s01-q08-i02.png](/assets/papers/the-perse-school/sample/specimen-paper-3/s01-q08-i02.png "papers/the-perse-school/sample/specimen-paper-3/s01-q08-i02.png")

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find the area of the region between the circles (labelled $R$ above).

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find the area of the region between the circles (labelled $R$ above).
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Area of square} = \text{side} \times \text{side}$

- ABBR: $\text{Area of circle} = \text{3.14} \times \text{radius} \times \text{radius}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Side of square} &= 2 \times 6 \\\\
                      &= 12 \ \text{cm} \\\\ 
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area}  &= \text{Area of square} - \text{Area of 4 quarter circle} \\\\
             &= 12 \times 12 - 4 \times \dfrac{1} {4}\times 6 \times 6 \times 3.14 \\\\
             &= 144 - \cancel 4 \times \dfrac{1} {\cancel 4}\times 6 \times 6 \times 3.14 \\\\
             &= 144 - 36 \times 3.14 \\\\
             &= 30.9 \ \text{cm}^2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$30.9 \ \text{cm}^2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find the radius of the largest circle that will fit in the region labelled $R$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find the radius of the largest circle that will fit in the region labelled $R$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Diagnol distance of the formed square} &= \sqrt{2} \times \text{side} \\\\
                                             &= \sqrt{2} \times 12 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Distance of R from center of circle}   &= \dfrac {12 \sqrt{2}} {2} \\\\
                                             &= \dfrac {6 \times 2 \times \sqrt{2}} {2} \\\\
                                             &= \dfrac {6 \times \cancel 2 \times \sqrt{2}} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                                             &= 6 \sqrt{2} \ \text{cm}                                          
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Largest radius that could fit}  &= \text{Distance of R from center of circle} - \text{Radius of the circle} \\\\
                                      &= 6 \sqrt{2} - 6  \\\\
                                      &= 6 (\sqrt{2} - 1) \\\\
                                      &= 2.48 \ \text{cm}                                         
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$ 2.48 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

If $r = 5$ and $h = 7$ , find $S$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If $r = 5$ and $h = 7$ , find $S$.
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">

%empty%
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}
S               &= \pi \ r^2 \ \sqrt{r^2+h^2} \\\\
S               &= \pi \times 5^2 \times \sqrt {5^2 + 7^2} \\\\
S               &= \pi \times 25 \times \sqrt {25 + 49} \\\\
S               &= 3.14 \times 25 \times \sqrt {74} \\\\
S               &= 675.2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Question**

If $𝑆 = 200$ and $r = 4$, find $h$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
S                                       &= \pi \ r^2 \ \sqrt{r^2+h^2} \\\\
200                                     &= 3.14 \times 4^2 \times \sqrt {4^2 + h^2} \\\\
200                                     &= 3.14 \times 16 \times \sqrt {16 +h^2} \\\\
3.14 \times 16 \times \sqrt {16 +h^2}   &= 200 \\\\
\sqrt {16 + h^2}                        &= \dfrac {200} {3.14 \times 16} \\\\
\sqrt {16 + h^2}                        &= \dfrac {25 \times 8} {3.14 \times 8 \times 2} \\\\
\sqrt {16 + h^2}                        &= \dfrac {25 \times \cancel 8} {3.14 \times \cancel 8 \times 2} \\\\
\sqrt {16 + h^2}                        &= \dfrac {25} {3.14 \times 2} \\\\
\sqrt {16 + h^2}                        &= \dfrac {25} {6.28} \\\\
\sqrt {16 + h^2}                        &= \dfrac {25} {6.28} \\\\
\sqrt {16 + h^2}                        &= 4 \\\\
16 + h^2                                &= 4^2 \\\\
h^2                                     &= 16 - 16 \\\\
h^2                                     &= 0 \\\\
h                                       &= 0
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If $S = 250$ and $h = 2r$ , find $r$ and $h$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
S                                       &= \pi \ r^2 \ \sqrt{r^2+h^2} \\\\
250                                     &= 3.14 \ r^2 \ \sqrt{r^2+(2r)^2} \\\\
250                                     &= 3.14 \times r^2 \times \sqrt{r^2 + 4r^2} \\\\
250                                     &= 3.14 \times r^2 \times \sqrt{5r^2} \\\\
250                                     &= 3.14 \times r^2 \times r \times \sqrt{5} \\\\
3.14 \times r^3 \times \sqrt{5}         &= 250 \\\\
r^3                                     &= \dfrac {250} {3.14 \times \sqrt{5}} \\\\
r^3                                     &= 35.6 \\\\ 
r                                       &= sqrt(3) {35.6} \\\\ 
r                                       &= 3.28 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
h       &= 2r \\\\
h       &= 2 \times 3.28 \\\\
h       &= 6.56
\end{aligned}
$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

$

**Question**

If $S = 2500$ and $r = 3.1$, find $R$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2\,\pi^2\,\times R \times 3.1 + 4\pi\,{3.1}^2                           &= 2500 \\\\
2 \times {3.14}^2 \times R \times 3.1 + 4 \times 3.14 \times {3.1}^2    &= 2500 \\\\
61.12 R + 120.70                                                        &= 2500 \\\\
61.12 R                                                                 &= 2500 - 120.70 \\\\
61.12 R                                                                 &= 2379.3 \\\\
R                                                                       &= \dfrac {2379.3} {61.12} \\\\
R                                                                       &= 39.01  
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

2 \times {3.14}^2 \times 10 \times 3.1 + 4 \times 3.14 \times r^2       &= 1800 \\\\
611.29 + 12.56 r                                                        &= 1800 \\\\
12.56 r^2                                                               &= 1800 - 611.29 \\\\
12.56 r^2                                                               &= 1188.71 \\\\
r^2                                                                     &= \dfrac {1188.71} {12.56} \\\\
r^2                                                                     &= 94.64 \\\\
r                                                                       &= \sqrt {94.64} \\\\
r                                                                       &= 9.7
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find the radius of the sphere with the same surface area as the cube.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find the radius of the sphere with the same surface area as the cube.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">

<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the radius of the sphere $= r$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
4\pi\,r^2       &= 150 \\\\
r^2             &= \dfrac {150} {4 \pi} \\\\
r^2             &= \dfrac {150} {4 \times 3.14} \\\\
r^2             &= \dfrac {150} {12.56} \\\\

r               &= \sqrt {12} \\\\
r               &= 3.46 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find the radius of the sphere with the same volume as the cube.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find the radius of the sphere with the same volume as the cube.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Surface area of cube} = 6 \times \text{edge} \times \text{edge}$

- ABBR: $\text{Volume of a cube} = (\text{Side}) ^ { 3 }$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the edge of the cube $= a$

Let the radius of the sphere $= r$
As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
6 \times a \times a     &= 150 \\\\
6a^2                    &= 150 \\\\
a^2                     &= \dfrac {150} {6} \\\\
a^2                     &= \dfrac {6 \times 25} {6} \\\\
a^2                     &= \dfrac {\cancel {6} \times 25} {\cancel {6}} \\\\
a^2                     &= 25 \\\\
a                       &= \sqrt {25} \\\\
a                       &= 5 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\dfrac{4} {3}\pi\,r^3   &= a^3 \\\\
\dfrac{4\pi} {3} r^3    &= 5^3 \\\\
r^3                     &= \dfrac {125 \times 3} {4\pi} \\\\
r^3                     &= \dfrac {30 \times 12.56} {12.56} \\\\
r^3                     &= \dfrac {30 \times \cancel {12.56}} {\cancel {12.56}} \\\\
r^3                     &= 30 \\\\
r                       &= \sqrt[3] {30} \\\\
r                       &= 3.1 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Radius of the sphere $= 3.1 \ \text{cm}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$3.1 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find the radius of the sphere if both the sphere and the cube have the same ratio of surface area to volume.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {4\pi\,r^2} {\dfrac{4} {3}\pi\,r^3}                           &= \dfrac {150} {125} \\\\
\dfrac {4\pi\,r^2 \times 3} {4\pi\,r^3}                             &= \dfrac {25 \times 6} {25 \times 5} \\\\
\dfrac {\cancel {4\pi}\,r^2 \times 3} {\cancel {4\pi}\,r^3}         &= \dfrac {\cancel {25} \times 6} {\cancel {25} \times 5} \\\\
r \times 3                                                          &= \dfrac {6} {5} \\\\
r                                                                   &= \dfrac {6} {5 \times 3} \\\\
r                                                                   &= \dfrac {2 \times 3} {5 \times 3} \\\\
r                                                                   &= \dfrac {2 \times \cancel {3}} {5 \times \cancel {3}} \\\\
r                                                                   &= \dfrac {2} {5} \\\\
r                                                                   &= 0.4 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Radius of the sphere $= 0.4 \ \text{cm}$
</div>

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area of shaded region}        &= \text{Area of square} - 2 \times \text{Area of AMC} - \text{Area of COD} \\\\
                                    &= a^2 - 2 \times \dfrac{1} {2} \times \dfrac{a} {2} \times a - \dfrac{1} {2} \times a \times \dfrac{a} {2} \\\\
                                    &= a^2 - \dfrac {2 \times a \times a} {2 \times 2} - \dfrac {a \times a} {2 \times 2} \\\\
                                    &= a^2 - \dfrac{2 \times a^2} {4} - \dfrac{a^2} {4} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac{4 \times a^2} {4} - \dfrac{2 \times a^2} {4} - \dfrac{a^2} {4} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac{4a^2 - 2a^2 - a^2} {4} \\\\
\text{Area of shaded region}        &= \dfrac{a^2} {4}
\end{aligned}
$

Fraction of area,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Fraction of shaded area}          &= \dfrac {\text{Area of shaded region}} {\text{Area of square}} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac{\dfrac{a^2} {4}} {a^2} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac{a^2} {4 \times a^2} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac{\cancel{a^2}} {4 \times \cancel{a^2}} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac{1} {4}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
